The location is right, but dense regular connective tissue, with collagen fibers in parallel rows, is the tissue of a tendon, not the epimysium. Choose dense regular if the question asked what a tendon is made of.
Correct. The epimysium covers the entire muscle and is made of dense irregular connective tissue.
This describes the endomysium, the fine areolar sheath with reticular fibers around each muscle fiber. It would be the answer for the covering of a single muscle cell.

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: What does the endomysium wrap, and what type of connective tissue is it?

Each myofibril; areolar connective tissue
The entire muscle; dense irregular connective tissue
Each muscle fiber; areolar connective tissue with reticular fibers

It is a fine areolar connective tissue reinforced with reticular fibers, a delicate mesh that holds capillaries and nerve endings right against each cell. You can see it on a cross section as the thin pale line between neighboring fibers.

Myofibrils are contractile rods inside the muscle cell, so no connective tissue can wrap them individually. Students choose this when they confuse the fiber (the cell) with the myofibril (a structure within the cell).
This describes the epimysium, the outer sheath around the whole muscle. It would be the answer if the question asked about the outermost covering.
Correct. The endomysium wraps each muscle fiber and is areolar connective tissue with reticular fibers.

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: How does the pull of a single muscle fiber get carried all the way to the bone?
options: Each muscle fiber has its own small tendon that attaches separately to bone
The sarcolemma of each fiber fuses directly with the bone at the insertion
Only the epimysium reaches the tendon, and the inner sheaths end within the belly
The three sheaths are continuous with one another and merge into the tendon
questions.why: The endomysium around each fiber is continuous with the perimysium around the fascicle, which is continuous with the epimysium around the whole muscle. At the end of the muscle all three blend together into the tendon, a cord of dense regular connective tissue that anchors to bone. Because the sheaths form one connected framework, the tug of every fiber is passed outward and on to the skeleton.
notes: Muscle fibers do not each have a private tendon. Their pull is gathered by the shared sheaths into one tendon or aponeurosis, so this is a misconception about how force is collected.
The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of the muscle cell and never attaches to bone directly. Muscle reaches bone only through connective tissue, the tendon or an aponeurosis.
The epimysium does merge into the tendon, but so do the perimysium and endomysium. If the inner sheaths stopped in the belly, the pull of individual fibers would never reach the bone.
Correct. The sheaths form one continuous connective tissue framework that becomes the tendon.

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: A sprinter can strain a hamstring by tearing fibers in the belly, or rupture its tendon so the muscle separates from bone. Which structural feature explains why a single forceful pull can injure either site?

The sarcoplasmic reticulum runs from the fibers into the tendon
The deep fascia binds neighboring muscles into one functional group
The superficial fascia connects the skin to the underlying muscle

A sudden overload stresses that whole line at once, and it fails at its weakest point. Sometimes that is the fibers and endomysium in the belly (a strain), and sometimes it is the tendon or its attachment (a rupture).

The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the calcium storing smooth ER inside each muscle fiber. It stays within the cell and has no part in the tendon, so it cannot transmit force to bone.

Deep fascia is the dense sheet that wraps and separates whole muscles and groups them by action. It would be the answer if the question asked what divides the limb into compartments, not what links a fiber to bone.
Superficial fascia is the subcutaneous layer of areolar and adipose tissue under the skin. It is the answer for what lies between the skin and muscles, but it does not carry muscle force to bone.

The muscle fiber

The pennate muscle, because many short, angled fascicles pack more fibers onto its tendon
Neither, because muscles of equal size always produce equal power
questions.why: In a pennate muscle, short fascicles attach at an angle to a central tendon like the barbs of a feather, so many more fibers fit into the same volume of muscle. More fibers pulling on the tendon means more power. The trade-off is range of motion: short, angled fascicles cannot move the insertion as far as the long fascicles of a parallel muscle.
notes: Shortening over a greater distance is a real advantage of parallel muscles, but it gives a larger range of motion, not more power. Pick this reasoning if the question asked which muscle moves its insertion farther.

Long, straight fascicles do pull in line with the tendon, but there are fewer of them per unit of muscle, so the total force is lower. Students pick this because a straight pull sounds more efficient.
Correct. Pennate muscles trade range of motion for power by packing in more fibers.
Size alone does not set power; how the fascicles are arranged decides how many fibers pull on the tendon. This choice ignores fascicle architecture entirely.
questions.answerText: The pennate muscle, because many short, angled fascicles pack more fibers onto its tendon

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: A needle is pushed from the surface of a muscle into its belly and stops between two fibers inside one fascicle. In order, which sheaths has it passed through, and which sheath surrounds its tip?
options: Perimysium, then epimysium; its tip sits in the endomysium.
Epimysium, then endomysium; its tip sits in the perimysium.
Epimysium, then perimysium; its tip sits in the endomysium.
Endomysium, then perimysium; its tip sits in the epimysium.
questions.why: The epimysium wraps the whole muscle, so the needle crosses it first. The perimysium wraps each fascicle, so the needle crosses it next to enter the bundle. Inside the fascicle, each fiber has its own fine endomysium, so the tip lies in the endomysium between neighboring fibers.
notes: The sheaths are named correctly, but the order is reversed. The epimysium is the outermost layer, so a needle from outside meets it first.
The endomysium wraps single fibers inside the fascicle, so the needle cannot cross it before the perimysium that wraps the whole fascicle.
Correct. Outside to inside, the sheaths run epimysium, perimysium, endomysium.
This runs from the inside out. The epimysium is the outer sheath around the whole muscle, so it cannot be where the tip ends up.
questions.answerText: Epimysium, then perimysium; its tip sits in the endomysium.
review: gross/histology tagged automatically from wording

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: Of the five levels of skeletal muscle organization, which two have no connective tissue sheath of their own?
options: The fascicle and the muscle fiber
The whole muscle and the fascicle
The muscle fiber and the myofibril
The myofibril and the myofilament
questions.why: Three levels are wrapped: the whole muscle in epimysium, each fascicle in perimysium, and each muscle fiber in endomysium. The myofibrils and myofilaments lie inside the fiber, so they have no connective tissue wrapping of their own.
notes: Both of these are wrapped. Each fascicle has perimysium and each muscle fiber has endomysium.
Both of these are wrapped. The whole muscle has epimysium and each fascicle has perimysium.
The myofibril has no sheath, but the muscle fiber does. Each fiber is wrapped in endomysium.
Correct. Myofibrils and myofilaments are inside the fiber and have no sheath.
review: gross/histology tagged automatically from wording

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: A cross section shows one structure wrapped in a fine areolar sheath, with many nuclei at its edge and hundreds of small rods filling its inside. Which level is the whole structure, and which level are the rods?
options: A fascicle filled with muscle fibers
A myofibril filled with myofilaments
A whole muscle filled with fascicles
A muscle fiber filled with myofibrils
questions.why: A fine areolar sheath with reticular fibers is the endomysium, which wraps a single muscle fiber, and many nuclei at the edge mark a multinucleated fiber. The rods filling it are myofibrils, the contractile rods that run the length of the fiber, with hundreds to thousands in each one.
notes: A fascicle is wrapped in perimysium, a dense irregular sheath, and it holds many whole fibers. It is not one cell with nuclei along its edge.
A myofibril sits inside a fiber, with no nuclei and no connective tissue sheath of its own. It is one of the rods here, not the structure holding them.
A whole muscle is wrapped in epimysium, which is dense irregular tissue, not a fine areolar sheath. It is an organ, not a single cell with nuclei along its edge.
Correct. Endomysium and edge nuclei mark one fiber, and the rods inside are myofibrils.
questions.answerText: A muscle fiber filled with myofibrils
review: gross/histology tagged automatically from wording

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: In Duchenne muscular dystrophy, dystrophin fails to link the thin filaments to the sarcolemma. Which two levels of muscle organization does this broken link connect?
options: The myofilament and the muscle fiber
The myofibril and the fascicle
The fascicle and the whole muscle
The muscle fiber and the fascicle
questions.why: Thin filaments are myofilaments, the smallest level, packed inside the myofibrils. The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber, a single muscle cell. Dystrophin bridges these two levels so the force of the sarcomere can reach the surface of the fiber and pass on to the connective tissue.
notes: Correct. Dystrophin links a myofilament to the membrane of its muscle fiber.
Thin filaments are the myofilament level inside the myofibril, and the sarcolemma belongs to a single fiber, not to a fascicle of many fibers.
Both of these levels are bundles of many fibers wrapped in connective tissue. Dystrophin works inside one cell, linking its filaments to its own membrane.
The sarcolemma does belong to the muscle fiber, but a thin filament is a myofilament, not a fascicle. A fascicle is a bundle of whole fibers.
questions.answerText: The myofilament and the muscle fiber
review: gross/histology tagged automatically from wording

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: An electron micrograph shows a long striped rod built of repeating units, each running from one Z disc to the next. Which level is the rod, and which levels lie just below and just above it?
options: A myofibril, with myofilaments below and a muscle fiber above
A myofilament, with sarcomeres below and a myofibril above
A muscle fiber, with myofibrils below and a fascicle above
A myofibril, with muscle fibers below and a fascicle above
questions.why: Sarcomeres, each from one Z disc to the next, repeat end to end along a myofibril, so the rod is a myofibril. The thick and thin myofilaments inside it are the next level down. Hundreds to thousands of myofibrils fill one muscle fiber, the next level up.
notes: Correct. The rod is a myofibril, between the myofilament and the muscle fiber.
A myofilament is a single thick or thin protein strand. Sarcomeres are built from overlapping myofilaments, so a sarcomere cannot be a level below a myofilament.
A muscle fiber is a whole cell holding many myofibrils. The repeating Z disc units describe one of its myofibrils, not the whole fiber.
The rod is a myofibril, but muscle fibers are larger, not smaller. Fibers contain myofibrils, and myofilaments are the level below.
questions.answerText: A myofibril, with myofilaments below and a muscle fiber above
review: gross/histology tagged automatically from wording

questions.topic: Muscle tissue types and muscle organization
questions.q: A slide labeled only as muscle shows cells that each have a single central nucleus. Which two tissues are still possible, and which feature on the slide would settle it?
options: Skeletal or cardiac; striations would mean skeletal.
Cardiac or smooth; striations would mean cardiac.
Skeletal or smooth; a central nucleus would mean smooth.
Cardiac or smooth; a spindle shape would mean cardiac.
questions.why: Cardiac muscle cells and smooth muscle cells each have one central nucleus, while skeletal fibers have many nuclei pushed to the edge. Of the two that remain, only cardiac muscle is striated, and its branching cells are joined by intercalated discs. Smooth muscle has spindle-shaped cells with no striations.
notes: Skeletal fibers have many nuclei at the edge, so a single central nucleus rules skeletal out. Skeletal and cardiac are both striated, so stripes would not separate them anyway.
Correct. A single central nucleus leaves cardiac or smooth, and only cardiac is striated.
Skeletal muscle is ruled out by the single central nucleus. The nucleus cannot be the deciding feature, because cardiac and smooth cells share it.
Cardiac and smooth are the right pair, but spindle-shaped cells mean smooth muscle. Cardiac cells are short and branching.
questions.answerText: Cardiac or smooth; striations would mean cardiac.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: The prefix sarco means flesh. Which statement correctly matches two sarco terms to the ordinary cell parts they name?
options: The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane, and the sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm
The sarcomere is the plasma membrane, and the sarcoplasm is the nucleus
The sarcolemma is the cytoplasm, and the sarcoplasm is the plasma membrane
The sarcolemma is the nucleus, and the sarcomere is the cytoplasm
questions.why: Muscle fibers have the same basic parts as other cells, but many of them carry the sarco prefix. The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane that wraps the fiber, and the sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm inside it. A helpful link is that lemma means husk or sheath, and plasm means the fluid material of the cell.
notes: Correct. The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane, and the sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm.

The sarcomere is the contractile unit of a myofibril, running from one Z disc to the next, and the sarcoplasm is cytoplasm, not a nucleus. Pick sarcomere for a question about the repeating unit that creates striations.
This swaps the two terms. The sarcolemma is the membrane on the outside of the fiber, and the sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm inside it.

The sarcolemma is a membrane, not a nucleus, and the sarcomere is a contractile unit, not cytoplasm. The nuclei of a muscle fiber are simply called nuclei (myonuclei) and sit just under the sarcolemma.
questions.answerText: The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane, and the sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: The prefix sarco in sarcolemma, sarcoplasm, and sarcomere comes from the Greek word for what?
options: Fiber
Cell
Flesh
Muscle
questions.why: Sarco comes from the Greek word for flesh, and it is attached to many structures of the muscle fiber. The sarcolemma is the fiber's plasma membrane, the sarcoplasm is its cytoplasm, and the sarcomere is the contractile unit of a myofibril. When you see sarco, you know the term names part of a muscle cell.
notes: Fiber is the meaning of the root fibr, as in fibroblast. It is tempting because skeletal muscle cells are called fibers, but sarco itself means flesh.
Cell is the meaning of the root cyto, as in cytoplasm. Students pick it because the sarco terms rename ordinary cell parts, but the prefix itself means flesh.
Correct. Sarco means flesh.
Muscle is the meaning of the roots myo and mys, as in myocardium and epimysium. Pick muscle for a question about those roots.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Where are the many nuclei of a skeletal muscle fiber located?
options: Just under the sarcolemma
In the center of the fiber
Inside the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Inside the myofibrils
questions.why: A skeletal muscle fiber is multinucleated, and its many nuclei are flattened against the inner surface of the sarcolemma, the fiber's plasma membrane. The middle of the fiber is packed with myofibrils, which leaves little room for nuclei there. Peripheral nuclei are one of the features that identify skeletal muscle on a slide.
notes: Correct. Skeletal muscle nuclei sit just under the sarcolemma.
A central nucleus is typical of cardiac and smooth muscle cells, each of which has one. Pick the center of the cell for a question about those tissues.
The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a network of tubules that stores calcium ions, and it does not hold nuclei. Pick it for a question about calcium storage in the fiber.
Myofibrils are contractile rods made of protein filaments, and they contain no nuclei. Pick myofibrils for a question about what fills most of the sarcoplasm.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is the cytoplasm of a muscle fiber called?
options: Sarcomere
Sarcoplasm
Sarcolemma
Sarcoplasmic reticulum
questions.why: The sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm of a muscle fiber, the material that fills the cell inside its plasma membrane. It holds the myofibrils, mitochondria, glycogen granules, and myoglobin. The name combines sarco, meaning flesh, with plasm, the term for the fluid contents of a cell.
notes: The sarcomere is the contractile unit of a myofibril, from one Z disc to the next. Pick it for a question about the repeating unit that creates striations.
Correct. The sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm of a muscle fiber.
The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane that wraps the fiber, not the material inside it. Pick it for a question about the muscle fiber's cell membrane.
The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the network of smooth endoplasmic reticulum inside the fiber that stores calcium. It sits within the sarcoplasm but is an organelle, not the cytoplasm itself.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is the plasma membrane of a muscle fiber called?
options: The sarcolemma
The sarcoplasm
The endomysium
The sarcoplasmic reticulum
questions.why: The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of a muscle fiber, the boundary of the cell. Its surface dives inward at regular intervals to form the T tubules, which carry signals deep into the fiber. Just outside the sarcolemma lies the endomysium, the connective tissue sheath around each fiber.
notes: Correct. The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber.
The sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm inside the fiber, not its membrane. Pick it for a question about the fluid material that holds the myofibrils.
The endomysium is a connective tissue sheath just outside the sarcolemma, not part of the cell itself. Pick it for a question about the sheath around each individual fiber.
The sarcoplasmic reticulum is an internal network of membrane tubules that stores calcium, not the outer cell membrane. Pick it for a question about calcium storage.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What are glycosomes in the sarcoplasm of a muscle fiber?
options: Organelles that produce most of the cell's ATP
Red pigment molecules that store oxygen
Sacs that store calcium ions
Granules of stored glycogen that supply glucose for energy
questions.why: Glycosomes are glycogen granules, small stores of carbohydrate fuel held in the sarcoplasm. When the muscle is active, the glycogen is broken down to glucose, which the cell uses to make ATP, the energy molecule contraction depends on. Muscle fibers hold far more of these granules than ordinary cells because their energy demand is so high.
notes: The organelles that produce most of the cell's ATP are mitochondria, packed in rows between the myofibrils. Glycosomes supply the fuel, but mitochondria do most of the ATP production.
A red pigment that stores oxygen is myoglobin, which also gives muscle its color. Pick myoglobin for a question about the muscle's oxygen store.
Sacs that store calcium ions are part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, especially its terminal cisterns. Pick those for a question about calcium storage.
Correct. Glycosomes are granules of stored glycogen.
questions.answerText: Granules of stored glycogen that supply glucose for energy

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which red pigment in the sarcoplasm stores oxygen and is similar to hemoglobin?
options: Glycogen
Myosin
Myoglobin
Melanin
questions.why: Myoglobin is a red, oxygen-binding pigment found in the sarcoplasm of muscle fibers. Like hemoglobin in red blood cells, it holds onto oxygen, but it stores the oxygen inside the muscle fiber where it can be used during activity. Myoglobin is also what gives muscle its red color.
notes: Glycogen is stored carbohydrate fuel held as granules in the sarcoplasm, and it is not a pigment. Pick glycogen for a question about the muscle's stored glucose.
Myosin is the protein that makes up the thick filaments inside a myofibril. The names look alike, but myosin is a contractile protein, not an oxygen store.
Correct. Myoglobin stores oxygen in the sarcoplasm.
Melanin is the brown to black pigment made by melanocytes in the epidermis of the skin. Pick it for a question about skin color.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which three specialized structures inside a skeletal muscle fiber are highly modified for contraction?
options: Myofibrils, sarcoplasmic reticulum, and T tubules
Nuclei, ribosomes, and centrioles
Myofibrils, Golgi apparatus, and lysosomes
Sarcomeres, fascicles, and endomysium
questions.why: Three structures in a muscle fiber are specialized for contraction. Myofibrils are the contractile rods, the sarcoplasmic reticulum is the network that stores calcium around each myofibril, and the T tubules are inward folds of the sarcolemma that carry the surface signal deep into the fiber. Together they let a large fiber contract quickly and as a unit.
notes: Correct. Myofibrils, sarcoplasmic reticulum, and T tubules are the specialized structures of the fiber.
Nuclei, ribosomes, and centrioles are general cell structures. Mature skeletal muscle fibers do have many nuclei, but none of these three is specially modified for contraction.
Myofibrils belong on the list, but the Golgi apparatus and lysosomes are ordinary organelles found in most cells. They are not the structures specially modified for contraction.

Fascicles and endomysium are outside the fiber: a fascicle is a bundle of fibers, and the endomysium is the sheath around each fiber. Sarcomeres are units within a myofibril rather than separate organelles.
questions.answerText: Myofibrils, sarcoplasmic reticulum, and T tubules

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Myofibrils fill most of a skeletal muscle fiber. About what share of the fiber's volume do they make up?
options: Nearly 100 percent
About 50 percent
About 20 percent
About 80 percent
questions.why: Myofibrils make up about 80 percent of a skeletal muscle fiber's volume. They run the full length of the fiber, packed side by side, with hundreds to thousands in each fiber. This dense packing is why the nuclei are pushed to the edge and the mitochondria are squeezed into rows between the myofibrils.
notes: The fiber still needs room for nuclei, mitochondria, sarcoplasmic reticulum, and glycogen, so myofibrils cannot fill all of it. Students choose this when they picture the fiber as nothing but contractile rods.
Half the volume underestimates how tightly myofibrils are packed. The other organelles are crowded into a much smaller share of the space.
Twenty percent is far too low for the contractile rods that fill the fiber. Students who pick this may be thinking of a minor organelle rather than the main contents of the cell.
Correct. Myofibrils make up about 80 percent of the fiber's volume.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is a myofibril?
options: A single muscle cell wrapped in endomysium
A contractile rod built of repeating sarcomeres
A bundle of fibers wrapped in perimysium
A single strand of actin or myosin protein
questions.why: A myofibril is a long, rod-shaped bundle of contractile proteins that runs the length of a muscle fiber. Each myofibril is a chain of sarcomeres, the repeating contractile units, and hundreds to thousands of myofibrils fill each fiber. In the levels of organization, the myofibril sits between the muscle fiber and the myofilament.
notes: A single muscle cell wrapped in endomysium is a muscle fiber, the level above the myofibril. Pick it for a question about what the endomysium surrounds.
Correct. A myofibril is a contractile rod inside the fiber, built of sarcomeres.
A bundle of fibers wrapped in perimysium is a fascicle, two levels above the myofibril. Pick it for a question about what the perimysium surrounds.
A single strand of actin or myosin is a myofilament, the level below the myofibril. Pick it for a question about the thick and thin filaments.
questions.answerText: A contractile rod built of repeating sarcomeres

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a specialized form of which organelle?
options: Golgi apparatus
Mitochondrion
Rough endoplasmic reticulum
Smooth endoplasmic reticulum
questions.why: The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the smooth endoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fiber, renamed with the sarco prefix. It has no ribosomes on its surface, which is what makes it smooth. In muscle it is specialized to wrap each myofibril and store calcium ions.
notes: The Golgi apparatus modifies, sorts, and packages proteins into vesicles. Pick it for a question about packaging cell products for secretion.
Mitochondria produce most of the cell's ATP and sit in rows between the myofibrils, but they are not related to the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Pick them for a question about energy production.
Rough endoplasmic reticulum is studded with ribosomes and makes proteins for export. Pick it for a question about the organelle that builds secreted proteins.
Correct. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is specialized smooth endoplasmic reticulum.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: How is the sarcoplasmic reticulum arranged relative to each myofibril?
options: As one large sac in the center of the fiber
As a network of tubules running lengthwise around each myofibril, like a sleeve
As a thin layer of connective tissue around the whole fiber
As tubes that dive straight inward from the sarcolemma across the fiber
questions.why: The sarcoplasmic reticulum forms a network of interconnecting tubules that wraps each myofibril like a loose sleeve, with most tubules running along the length of the myofibril. This arrangement keeps the calcium store close to every part of every myofibril. At regular intervals the network widens into terminal cisterns that sit beside the T tubules.
notes: A single central sac would leave most myofibrils far from the calcium store. The network instead surrounds every myofibril, which is why it works as a sleeve.
Correct. The sarcoplasmic reticulum wraps each myofibril like a sleeve.
A connective tissue layer around the whole fiber is the endomysium, which lies outside the cell. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is an organelle inside the fiber.
Tubes diving straight inward from the sarcolemma are T tubules, which run across the fiber rather than along each myofibril. Pick this description for a question about T tubules.
questions.answerText: As a network of tubules running lengthwise around each myofibril, like a sleeve

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What are the enlarged end sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum called?
options: T tubules
Terminal cisterns
Myofibrils
Glycosomes
questions.why: Terminal cisterns (also called terminal cisternae) are the enlarged sacs at the ends of the sarcoplasmic reticulum's tubules. They always occur in pairs, one on each side of a T tubule, and together with that T tubule they form a triad. Because they are part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, they hold stored calcium ions.
notes: T tubules are inward folds of the sarcolemma, not part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum. A T tubule sits between two terminal cisterns, so pick it for a question about the middle tube of a triad.
Correct. The enlarged end sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum are terminal cisterns.
Myofibrils are the contractile rods that the sarcoplasmic reticulum wraps around. Pick them for a question about what fills most of the fiber.
Glycosomes are granules of stored glycogen in the sarcoplasm, not membrane sacs. Pick them for a question about the muscle's carbohydrate fuel.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: In skeletal muscle, the terminal cisterns form cross channels at which location along the sarcomere?
options: At the center of the Z disc
At each junction of an A band and an I band
At the M line
Within the H zone
questions.why: The terminal cisterns form channels that run across the myofibril where each dark A band meets a light I band. A T tubule also dives into the fiber at each of these junctions, so the paired terminal cisterns and the T tubule form a triad there. Each sarcomere therefore has two triads, one at each A band and I band junction.
notes: The Z disc is the protein plate at each end of the sarcomere that anchors the thin filaments. Pick it for a question about the border of a sarcomere.
Correct. Terminal cisterns sit at the A band and I band junctions.
The M line is the protein line at the center of the H zone that anchors the thick filaments. Pick it for a question about what holds the thick filaments together.

The H zone is the lighter region in the center of the A band with thick filaments only. It is where the sarcoplasmic reticulum tubules connect with each other, not where the terminal cisterns form their cross channels.
questions.answerText: At each junction of an A band and an I band

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: In one line, what is the main role of the sarcoplasmic reticulum in a muscle fiber?
options: It carries the surface signal deep into the fiber
It produces most of the fiber's ATP
It stores oxygen for the fiber
It stores calcium ions and releases them into the sarcoplasm
questions.why: The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the calcium store of the muscle fiber. It holds calcium ions (Ca2+) inside its tubules and terminal cisterns and releases them into the sarcoplasm when the fiber is stimulated, which allows contraction to happen. Its sleeve-like arrangement keeps this store close to every myofibril.
notes: Carrying the surface signal deep into the fiber is the job of the T tubules, which are inward folds of the sarcolemma. Pick T tubules for that question.
Most of the fiber's ATP comes from mitochondria, packed in rows between the myofibrils. Pick mitochondria for a question about energy production.
Oxygen is stored by myoglobin, a red pigment in the sarcoplasm. Pick myoglobin for a question about the fiber's oxygen store.
Correct. The sarcoplasmic reticulum stores and releases calcium ions.
questions.answerText: It stores calcium ions and releases them into the sarcoplasm

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is a T tubule?
options: A contractile rod running the length of the fiber
An inward extension of the sarcolemma that runs deep into the fiber
A capillary running between neighboring muscle fibers
An enlarged end sac of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
questions.why: A T tubule, or transverse tubule, is a narrow tunnel formed where the sarcolemma dives inward, running across the fiber at right angles to its length. Because it is continuous with the sarcolemma, it carries the signal that arrives at the cell surface deep into the interior of the fiber. Each T tubule runs between a pair of terminal cisterns.
notes: A contractile rod running the length of the fiber is a myofibril. Pick it for a question about what fills most of the sarcoplasm.
Correct. A T tubule is an inward extension of the sarcolemma.
Capillaries run outside the fibers in the endomysium and carry blood, not signals. Pick capillaries for a question about blood supply to the fibers.
An enlarged end sac of the sarcoplasmic reticulum is a terminal cistern. Pick it for a question about the sacs on either side of a T tubule.
questions.answerText: An inward extension of the sarcolemma that runs deep into the fiber

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Between which structures does a T tubule run?
options: Between two Z discs of one sarcomere
Between two neighboring muscle fibers
Between two terminal cisterns of the sarcoplasmic reticulum
Between the thick and thin filaments of a myofibril
questions.why: Each T tubule passes between a pair of terminal cisterns, the enlarged sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum. One T tubule plus the two terminal cisterns beside it forms a triad. This places the surface signal carried by the T tubule right next to the calcium stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
notes: The space between two Z discs is one sarcomere, the contractile unit of a myofibril. Pick this for a question about the length of a sarcomere.
The space between neighboring fibers is filled by endomysium, the connective tissue sheath around each fiber. T tubules are inside a single fiber.
Correct. A T tubule runs between two terminal cisterns.
Thick and thin filaments overlap inside the myofibril, and no T tubule runs between them. Pick this for a question about the zone of overlap in a sarcomere.
questions.answerText: Between two terminal cisterns of the sarcoplasmic reticulum

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which structures make up a triad?
options: One terminal cistern and two mitochondria
One T tubule and two terminal cisterns
Two T tubules and one terminal cistern
One myofibril and two Z discs
questions.why: A triad is a set of three structures: one T tubule in the middle with a terminal cistern of the sarcoplasmic reticulum on each side. It is the meeting point where the surface signal carried by the T tubule reaches the calcium store of the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Triads repeat along every myofibril at each A band and I band junction.
notes: Mitochondria lie in rows between the myofibrils, but they are not part of a triad. A triad is made only of the T tubule and the two sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
Correct. A triad is one T tubule flanked by two terminal cisterns.
This reverses the count. Terminal cisterns always come in pairs, and the single T tubule sits between them.
A myofibril with Z discs describes the contractile rod and the borders of its sarcomeres. Pick this for a question about the structure of a myofibril, not a triad.
questions.answerText: One T tubule and two terminal cisterns

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A structure is described as a single long, cylindrical cell with many peripheral nuclei, wrapped in endomysium. Which level of muscle organization is it?
options: The myofibril
The fascicle
The muscle fiber
The sarcomere
questions.why: A muscle fiber is one skeletal muscle cell. It is long and cylindrical, carries many nuclei just under the sarcolemma, and is wrapped in its own endomysium. It sits between the fascicle (a bundle of fibers) above it and the myofibril (a contractile rod inside it) below it.
notes: A myofibril is a contractile rod inside the fiber, and it has no nuclei of its own. Pick it for a question about the level just below the fiber.
A fascicle is a bundle of many fibers wrapped in perimysium, not a single cell. Pick it for a question about the level above the fiber.
Correct. A single multinucleated cell wrapped in endomysium is a muscle fiber.
A sarcomere is the repeating contractile unit of a myofibril, from one Z disc to the next. Pick it for a question about the smallest unit that contracts.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which statement correctly compares myoglobin and glycosomes in a muscle fiber?
options: Myoglobin stores oxygen, and glycosomes store glycogen as a source of glucose
Myoglobin stores calcium ions, and glycosomes store oxygen
Both store oxygen, but only myoglobin is red
Myoglobin stores glycogen, and glycosomes store oxygen
questions.why: A working muscle fiber needs both oxygen and fuel to make ATP. Myoglobin, a red pigment in the sarcoplasm, stores oxygen. Glycosomes are granules of glycogen that are broken down to glucose when the fiber is active, supplying the fuel side of energy production.
notes: Correct. Myoglobin stores oxygen and glycosomes store glycogen.
Calcium ions are stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum, not by myoglobin, and glycosomes store fuel rather than oxygen. Pick the sarcoplasmic reticulum for a question about calcium storage.
Only myoglobin binds oxygen. Glycosomes are fuel stores made of glycogen, so this statement gives them a job they do not have.
This swaps the two. Myoglobin is the oxygen-binding pigment, and glycosomes are the glycogen granules.
questions.answerText: Myoglobin stores oxygen, and glycosomes store glycogen as a source of glucose

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Why do the mitochondria and other organelles look squashed in a skeletal muscle fiber?
options: Densely packed myofibrils crowd the other organelles into the spaces between them
The endomysium presses in on the fiber from outside
The many nuclei take up most of the center of the fiber
The sarcolemma shrinks around the organelles during contraction
questions.why: Myofibrils make up about 80 percent of a skeletal muscle fiber's volume. With so much space taken by these contractile rods, the mitochondria and other organelles are squeezed into the narrow gaps between them. This crowding is why the organelles look flattened and why the mitochondria line up in rows.
notes: Correct. Densely packed myofibrils crowd the other organelles.
The endomysium is a delicate areolar sheath that does not compress the fiber. The crowding comes from inside the cell, from the myofibrils.
The nuclei of a skeletal muscle fiber are pushed to the edge, just under the sarcolemma, not in the center. They are themselves crowded aside by the myofibrils.
The sarcolemma does not shrink around the organelles; the fiber keeps its volume. Students choose this when they picture contraction squeezing the cell from the outside.
questions.answerText: Densely packed myofibrils crowd the other organelles into the spaces between them

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which structure carries the signal that arrives at the sarcolemma deep into the interior of the muscle fiber?
options: The endomysium
The T tubule
The terminal cistern
The myofibril
questions.why: T tubules are narrow tunnels of the sarcolemma that dive into the fiber at right angles to its length. Because they are continuous with the surface membrane, they carry the surface signal deep into the cell. This lets the signal reach the sarcoplasmic reticulum around every myofibril at almost the same moment.
notes: The endomysium is a connective tissue sheath outside the fiber. It carries capillaries and nerve branches to the fiber, but it does not carry signals into the cell's interior.
Correct. The T tubule carries the surface signal deep into the fiber.
A terminal cistern is an enlarged sac of the sarcoplasmic reticulum that stores calcium. It receives the signal brought by the T tubule beside it rather than carrying it inward.
A myofibril is a contractile rod that shortens in response to the signal, not the pathway that carries it. Pick it for a question about what fills most of the fiber.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which sarco term names the contractile unit of a myofibril, running from one Z disc to the next?
options: The sarcolemma
The sarcomere
The sarcoplasmic reticulum
The sarcoplasm
questions.why: The sarcomere is the contractile unit of muscle, the segment of a myofibril from one Z disc to the next. Thousands of sarcomeres line up end to end along each myofibril, and their repeating light and dark bands create the striations of skeletal muscle. The name combines sarco, flesh, with mere, meaning part.
notes: The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane of the muscle fiber. Pick it for a question about the fiber's cell membrane.
Correct. The sarcomere is the unit from one Z disc to the next.
The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the smooth endoplasmic reticulum that wraps each myofibril and stores calcium. Pick it for a question about calcium storage.
The sarcoplasm is the cytoplasm of the muscle fiber. Pick it for a question about the fluid that holds the myofibrils.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which even smaller structures make up a myofibril?
options: T tubules
Terminal cisterns
Myofilaments
Fascicles
questions.why: Each myofibril is built from myofilaments, the thick and thin protein strands that are the smallest level of muscle organization. Thick filaments are made mainly of myosin and thin filaments mainly of actin. Their orderly overlap forms the sarcomeres that repeat along the myofibril.
notes: T tubules are inward folds of the sarcolemma that run between myofibrils, not inside them. Pick them for a question about how the surface signal reaches the fiber's interior.
Terminal cisterns are sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum that sit outside the myofibril, wrapped around it. Pick them for a question about the parts of a triad.
Correct. Myofibrils are made of myofilaments.
Fascicles are bundles of muscle fibers, which makes them much larger than a myofibril. Pick fascicles for a question about what the perimysium wraps.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Most tubules of the sarcoplasmic reticulum run lengthwise along the myofibril. At which region of the sarcomere do they connect with one another?
options: At the H zone
At each A band and I band junction
At the Z disc
Within the I band
questions.why: The longitudinal tubules of the sarcoplasmic reticulum run along the myofibril and connect with each other in the region of the H zone, the lighter center of the A band. At the A band and I band junctions, the network widens into terminal cisterns that sit beside the T tubules. Knowing these two landmarks helps you picture the sleeve of sarcoplasmic reticulum around each sarcomere.
notes: Correct. The sarcoplasmic reticulum tubules connect with each other at the H zone.
The A band and I band junctions are where the terminal cisterns and T tubules form triads. Pick this location for a question about where triads are found.
The Z disc is the protein plate at each end of the sarcomere that anchors the thin filaments. Pick it for a question about the border of a sarcomere.
The I band is the light band of thin filaments only, with a Z disc through its center. Pick it for a question about the region of a sarcomere that contains only thin filaments.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which pair of structures is found in large numbers around the myofibrils and sarcoplasmic reticulum, supplying energy for contraction?
options: Ribosomes and lysosomes
Mitochondria and glycogen granules
Nuclei and centrioles
T tubules and terminal cisterns
questions.why: Contraction uses a great deal of ATP, so the fiber packs energy-producing structures close to where they are needed. Mitochondria, which make most of the ATP, sit in rows between the myofibrils, and glycogen granules supply the glucose fuel. Both cluster around the myofibrils and sarcoplasmic reticulum.
notes: Ribosomes build proteins and lysosomes digest worn-out material. They are found in muscle fibers but are not the structures supplying energy for contraction.
Correct. Mitochondria and glycogen granules supply the energy for contraction.
Nuclei in a skeletal muscle fiber are pushed to the edge under the sarcolemma, and centrioles organize cell division. Neither supplies energy for contraction.
T tubules and terminal cisterns form the triads that bring the signal next to the calcium store. They help start contraction but do not supply its energy.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Terminal cisterns are enlarged parts of which structure?
options: The sarcolemma
The sarcoplasmic reticulum
The T tubule
The myofibril
questions.why: Terminal cisterns are the enlarged end sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, the smooth endoplasmic reticulum of the muscle fiber. They sit in pairs on either side of a T tubule. Students often confuse which part of the triad belongs to which membrane system, so remember that the two side sacs belong to the sarcoplasmic reticulum and the middle tube is an inward fold of the sarcolemma.
notes: The sarcolemma is the plasma membrane, and its inward folds form the T tubules, not the terminal cisterns. Pick it for a question about what the T tubules are continuous with.
Correct. Terminal cisterns are part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
The T tubule is the middle tube of the triad, flanked by the terminal cisterns but not part of the same membrane system. Pick it for a question about the inward folds of the sarcolemma.
A myofibril is the contractile rod that the sarcoplasmic reticulum wraps around. It contains myofilaments, not membrane sacs.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which list orders the levels of organization from a whole muscle fiber down to the smallest level?
options: Myofilament, myofibril, muscle fiber
Muscle fiber, myofilament, myofibril
Muscle fiber, myofibril, myofilament
Myofibril, muscle fiber, myofilament
questions.why: A muscle fiber is a single cell, and inside it are hundreds to thousands of myofibrils, the contractile rods. Each myofibril, in turn, is built of myofilaments, the thick and thin protein strands. Going from the fiber downward, the order is fiber, myofibril, myofilament.
notes: This list is the right sequence read from smallest to largest. Pick it if the question asks you to build up from the smallest level to the whole fiber.
Myofilaments make up myofibrils, so they are smaller and must come last. This order swaps the last two levels.
Correct. The order from fiber downward is muscle fiber, myofibril, myofilament.
The myofibril is inside the fiber, so it cannot come before the fiber when moving downward in size. This order swaps the first two levels.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: On an electron micrograph, a technician finds one narrow central tube flanked by two larger sacs at an A band and I band junction. Which structure is this?
options: A myofibril
A triad
A sarcomere
An intercalated disc
questions.why: One central tube with a larger sac on each side is a triad. The central tube is a T tubule, an inward fold of the sarcolemma, and the two sacs are terminal cisterns of the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Triads sit at each A band and I band junction, which matches where the technician found this one.
notes: A myofibril is a long contractile rod made of sarcomeres, much longer than the small cluster described here. Pick it for a question about what the sarcoplasmic reticulum wraps around.
Correct. One T tubule flanked by two terminal cisterns is a triad.
A sarcomere is the segment of a myofibril from one Z disc to the next, made of overlapping filaments rather than a tube and sacs. Pick it for a question about the repeating contractile unit.
An intercalated disc is the junction joining two cardiac muscle cells end to end. Pick it for a question about how cardiac cells connect, not about structures inside a skeletal muscle fiber.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A skeletal muscle fiber is a very large cell, yet the whole fiber responds almost at once when stimulated. Why is the triad important for this?
options: It anchors the thick filaments at the sarcomere center
It connects the muscle fiber to its tendon
It joins neighboring fibers so they contract together
It puts the T tubule's signal beside the calcium store
questions.why: The triad is the structural meeting point where a surface signal reaches the calcium store. The T tubule carries the signal from the sarcolemma deep into the fiber, and the two terminal cisterns beside it hold the calcium. Because triads repeat tightly along every myofibril, the signal reaches the calcium store throughout the whole fiber almost at the same moment.
notes: Anchoring the thick filaments at the center of the sarcomere is the job of the M line. Pick the M line for that question.
The connection from muscle to tendon is made by the connective tissue sheaths, which merge into the tendon. Pick the sheaths for a question about how a fiber's pull reaches the bone.
Skeletal muscle fibers are not joined to each other electrically. Cells joined so they contract together describes the intercalated discs of cardiac muscle.
Correct. The triad places the T tubule's signal beside the calcium store of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
questions.answerText: It puts the T tubule's signal beside the calcium store

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A muscle that resists fatigue looks deep red when sectioned. Which component of its sarcoplasm chiefly accounts for the red color and the stored oxygen?
options: Collagen
Myoglobin
Glycogen
Myosin
questions.why: Myoglobin is a red, oxygen-binding pigment in the sarcoplasm. Muscles with a lot of myoglobin look deep red and can keep working for a long time, because they have a steady supply of stored oxygen for making ATP. Muscle with little myoglobin looks paler.
notes: Collagen is the main fiber of the connective tissue sheaths and tendons, which look white rather than red. Pick it for a question about what makes tendons strong.
Correct. Myoglobin gives muscle its red color and stores oxygen.
Glycogen is stored carbohydrate fuel and has no red color. Pick it for a question about the muscle's stored glucose.
Myosin is the protein of the thick filaments, and it is not a pigment. The similar name makes it easy to confuse with myoglobin.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A student confuses the T tubule with the sarcoplasmic reticulum. Which statement correctly tells them apart?
options: The T tubule is smooth endoplasmic reticulum that stores calcium, while the sarcoplasmic reticulum is an inward extension of the sarcolemma
The T tubule is an inward extension of the sarcolemma that carries the surface signal inward, while the sarcoplasmic reticulum is smooth endoplasmic reticulum that stores calcium
Both are parts of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, but only the T tubule stores calcium
Both are inward extensions of the sarcolemma, but only the sarcoplasmic reticulum reaches the myofibrils
questions.why: The T tubule and the sarcoplasmic reticulum come from different membranes and do different jobs. The T tubule is part of the sarcolemma, folded inward to carry the surface signal deep into the fiber. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is the fiber's smooth endoplasmic reticulum, wrapped around each myofibril to store calcium. At a triad, one T tubule sits between two terminal cisterns of the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
notes: This swaps the two structures. The T tubule is the inward fold of the sarcolemma, and the sarcoplasmic reticulum is the calcium store.
Correct. The T tubule comes from the sarcolemma and carries the signal, while the sarcoplasmic reticulum stores calcium.
The T tubule is not part of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, and it does not store calcium. Only the sarcoplasmic reticulum, including its terminal cisterns, stores calcium.
Only the T tubule is an extension of the sarcolemma. The sarcoplasmic reticulum is a separate internal organelle.
questions.answerText: The T tubule is an inward extension of the sarcolemma that carries the surface signal inward, while the sarcoplasmic reticulum is smooth endoplasmic reticulum that stores calcium

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which structural protein links the thin filaments to the sarcolemma and is faulty in Duchenne muscular dystrophy?
options: Titin
Dystrophin
Myomesin
Nebulin
questions.why: Dystrophin links the thin filaments of the sarcomere to the sarcolemma, so the force of contraction is passed from the sarcomere out to the connective tissue. In Duchenne muscular dystrophy the gene for dystrophin is faulty, so this link fails. The fiber then damages itself with ordinary use, which causes progressive weakness.
notes: Titin spans from the Z disc to the M line, anchoring the thick filament and giving the sarcomere elastic recoil. Pick it for a question about what keeps the sarcomere from overstretching.
Correct. Dystrophin links the thin filaments to the sarcolemma and is faulty in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.
Myomesin is found at the M line, where it binds the thick filaments together. Pick it for a question about the protein of the M line.
Nebulin runs along the thin filament, anchoring it and setting its length. Pick it for a question about what determines thin filament length.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which structural protein spans from the Z disc to the M line, anchors the thick filament, and gives the sarcomere elastic recoil?
options: Nebulin
Titin
Dystrophin
Alpha-actinin
questions.why: Titin is a giant structural protein that stretches from the Z disc to the M line. It anchors each thick filament in place, and its spring-like structure gives the sarcomere elastic recoil and keeps it from being overstretched. Titin helps explain the property of elasticity at the level of the sarcomere.
notes: Nebulin runs along the thin filament, anchoring it and setting its length. Pick it for a question about thin filament length.
Correct. Titin spans from the Z disc to the M line and gives the sarcomere elastic recoil.
Dystrophin links the thin filaments to the sarcolemma and is faulty in Duchenne muscular dystrophy. Pick it for a question about that disease.
Alpha-actinin is located in the Z disc, where it binds the thin filaments and titin to the disc. Pick it for a question about the protein of the Z disc.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A histologist wants to confirm that a cell is a skeletal muscle fiber rather than a cardiac muscle cell. Which nuclear feature identifies the skeletal fiber?
options: No nuclei at all
One nucleus in the center of the cell
Two nuclei, one at each end of the cell
Many nuclei just under the sarcolemma
questions.why: Skeletal muscle fibers form when many embryonic cells fuse, so each fiber has many nuclei, and these are pushed to the edge just under the sarcolemma. A cardiac muscle cell has one central nucleus. Counting and locating the nuclei is one of the quickest ways to tell the two striated tissues apart.
notes: Mature red blood cells have no nucleus, but every muscle cell does. Students choose this when they confuse muscle cells with formed elements of the blood.
One central nucleus is the pattern of a cardiac muscle cell, and of a smooth muscle cell too. Pick it for a question that asks how to identify cardiac muscle.
No muscle cell places its nuclei at its two ends. Students choose this when they picture a long fiber and guess that its nuclei must sit at the tips.
Correct. Many peripheral nuclei identify a skeletal muscle fiber.
questions.answerText: Many nuclei just under the sarcolemma

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Where are the mitochondria located in a skeletal muscle fiber?
options: Inside the terminal cisterns
Clustered at the center of each myofibril
In rows between the myofibrils
Inside the T tubules
questions.why: Mitochondria in a skeletal muscle fiber are packed in rows between the myofibrils. The myofibrils take up about 80 percent of the fiber's volume, so the mitochondria are squeezed into the narrow spaces between them. This places the ATP they produce right beside the contractile machinery that uses it.
notes: Terminal cisterns are sacs of the sarcoplasmic reticulum that store calcium, not mitochondria. Pick them for a question about the parts of a triad.
A myofibril is a tightly packed rod of myofilaments, with no room for organelles inside it. The mitochondria lie alongside the myofibrils, not within them.
Correct. Mitochondria lie in rows between the myofibrils.
T tubules are narrow inward folds of the sarcolemma that carry the surface signal, and they do not contain organelles. Pick them for a question about how the signal reaches the fiber's interior.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is a sarcomere?
options: One T tubule flanked by two terminal cisternae
A bundle of muscle fibers wrapped in perimysium
A single long, multinucleated muscle cell
The segment of a myofibril from one Z disc to the next
questions.why: A sarcomere is the contractile unit of skeletal muscle. It is one segment of a myofibril, running from one Z disc (the protein plate at its border) to the next. Thousands of sarcomeres repeat end to end along every myofibril, and their bands line up to produce the stripes seen in skeletal muscle.
notes: This describes a triad, the meeting point of a T tubule and the sarcoplasmic reticulum. It would be the answer for a question about where the surface signal reaches the calcium store.
This describes a fascicle, a level of organization far larger than a sarcomere. Pick the fascicle if the question asked what the perimysium wraps.
This describes a muscle fiber, the whole cell. A fiber contains myofibrils, and each myofibril is built of thousands of sarcomeres, so the fiber is many levels larger.
Correct. The sarcomere is the repeating contractile unit, bordered by a Z disc at each end.
questions.answerText: The segment of a myofibril from one Z disc to the next

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A sarcomere extends between which two structures?
options: Two M lines
Two H zones
Two A bands
Two Z discs
questions.why: The sarcomere is defined by its borders, the Z discs. Each Z disc is a protein plate that anchors the thin filaments, and the stretch of myofibril from one Z disc to the next is one sarcomere. Everything else, the A band, H zone, and M line, sits inside that segment.
notes: The M line sits in the center of the sarcomere, where it anchors the thick filaments. Students mix it up with the Z disc because both are thin dark lines, but the M line marks the middle, not the border.
The H zone is the lighter region in the center of the A band, holding thick filaments only. Each sarcomere has just one H zone, in its middle, so it cannot mark the borders.
The A band is the dark band in the middle of the sarcomere. It would be the answer if the question asked which band is as wide as the thick filaments are long.
Correct. A Z disc forms each border of the sarcomere.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What produces the striations (stripes) seen along a skeletal muscle myofibril?
options: Rows of mitochondria between myofibrils
Alternating dark A bands and light I bands
Branching fibers joined end to end
Layers of endomysium around each fiber
questions.why: Striations come from the sarcomeres. Each sarcomere has a dark A band, where the thick filaments lie, and light I bands, where only thin filaments lie. Because thousands of sarcomeres are lined up in register across the fiber, these bands appear as continuous stripes under the microscope.
notes: Mitochondria do sit in rows between myofibrils, where they supply ATP for contraction, but they do not create the banding pattern. They would be the answer if the question asked what supplies the energy for contraction.
Correct. The repeating A and I bands of aligned sarcomeres create the stripes.
Branching fibers joined by intercalated discs describe cardiac muscle. Cardiac muscle is also striated, but the branching is not what makes the stripes; its sarcomeres do.

The endomysium is the fine connective tissue sheath around each muscle fiber. It wraps the outside of the cell and has nothing to do with the bands inside it. Pick it if the question asked which sheath wraps a single fiber.
questions.answerText: Alternating dark A bands and light I bands

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which band of the sarcomere is the dark band?
options: The I band
The A band
The Z disc
The H zone
questions.why: The A band is the dark band of the sarcomere. It is as wide as the thick filaments are long, and the dense myosin of those filaments, overlapped at each edge by thin filaments, makes it stain darkly. The alternating dark A bands and light I bands produce the striations of skeletal muscle.
notes: The I band is the light band, containing thin filaments only. Pick it if the question asked which band is pale or which band a Z disc runs through.
Correct. The A band is the dark band because it holds the thick filaments.
The Z disc is a protein plate at the border of the sarcomere, seen as a thin line, not a band. Pick it if the question asked what anchors the thin filaments or marks each end of the sarcomere.
The H zone is a lighter region in the center of the A band, where thick filaments lie without thin filament overlap. It would be the answer for the region of thick filaments only.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which band of the sarcomere is the light band?
options: The A band
The I band
The H zone
The M line
questions.why: The I band is the light band of the sarcomere. It contains only thin filaments, which are less dense than the thick filaments of the A band, so it appears pale. A Z disc runs through the center of each I band, which means one I band is shared between two neighboring sarcomeres.
notes: The A band is the dark band, holding the thick filaments across its full width. It would be the answer for the dark band or the band that never changes width during contraction.
Correct. The I band is light because it contains thin filaments only.
The H zone is a lighter area, but it lies in the center of the dark A band, not between A bands. Pick it for the region that contains thick filaments only.
The M line is a protein line in the middle of the H zone that anchors the thick filaments to one another. It is a line, not a band, and it marks the center of the sarcomere.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is the lighter region in the center of the dark A band called?
options: The I band
The zone of overlap
The Z disc
The H zone
questions.why: The H zone is the lighter region in the middle of the A band. Here the thick filaments lie without any thin filaments overlapping them, so the region looks paler than the edges of the A band, where both filaments overlap. The M line runs through the center of the H zone.
notes: The I band is also light, but it lies outside the A band, between two A bands, with a Z disc through its center. Pick it for the light band that contains thin filaments only.
The zone of overlap is at each end of the A band, where thick and thin filaments interleave. Because it holds both filaments, it is the darkest part of the A band, the opposite of the pale H zone.
The Z disc is the protein plate at the border of the sarcomere. It runs through the I band, not the A band, and anchors the thin filaments.
Correct. The H zone is the paler center of the A band.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which line runs through the center of the H zone?
options: The A band
The zone of overlap
The Z disc
The M line
questions.why: The M line is a protein line in the exact center of the sarcomere, running through the middle of the H zone. Its job is structural: it anchors the thick filaments to one another so they stay aligned. The protein myomesin forms much of the M line.
notes: The A band is the dark band that contains the H zone, so it surrounds the H zone rather than running through its middle. It would be the answer for the band as wide as the thick filaments are long.
The zone of overlap lies at each edge of the A band, where thick and thin filaments interleave. It flanks the H zone on both sides instead of bisecting it.
The Z disc runs through the center of the I band and marks the border of the sarcomere. Pick it if the question asked which line bisects the I band.
Correct. The M line bisects the H zone and marks the center of the sarcomere.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which protein is found at the M line, binding the thick filaments together?
options: Myomesin
Alpha-actinin
Titin
Tropomyosin
questions.why: Myomesin is a structural protein located at the M line, in the center of the sarcomere. It binds neighboring thick filaments together so they stay evenly spaced and lined up. Remember the pairing by the shared letter: Myomesin at the M line, while alpha-actinin works at the Z disc.
notes: Correct. Myomesin sits at the M line and holds the thick filaments together.
Alpha-actinin is found at the Z disc, where it binds the thin filaments and titin. It is the right answer for the protein at the border of the sarcomere, not at its center.

Titin attaches at the M line, but it spans the whole half sarcomere from the Z disc to the M line, acting as an elastic spring. Pick titin if the question asked which protein gives the sarcomere elastic recoil.

Tropomyosin is a regulatory protein lying along the thin filament, covering the myosin-binding sites on actin in relaxed muscle. It never reaches the M line, because thin filaments do not extend into the H zone.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: The Z disc runs through the center of which band?
options: The I band
The zone of overlap
The H zone
The A band
questions.why: The Z disc is the protein plate at each border of a sarcomere, and it runs through the middle of the light I band. That placement means half of every I band belongs to one sarcomere and half to the next. Thin filaments extend from the Z disc in both directions, which is why the I band on either side contains thin filaments only.
notes: Correct. The Z disc bisects the I band, so each I band is split between two sarcomeres.
The zone of overlap is where thick and thin filaments interleave at each end of the A band. No line runs through it; the Z disc lies farther out, in the middle of the I band.

The H zone is the pale center of the A band, and the line through its middle is the M line. Students mix up the two central lines; the M line belongs to the H zone, while the Z disc belongs to the I band.
The A band is the dark central band of the sarcomere, bisected by the H zone and M line, not by the Z disc. Pick it if the question asked which band holds the thick filaments.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What are myofilaments?
options: Tunnels of sarcolemma that dive into the fiber
The thick and thin protein strands within a myofibril
The long contractile rods that fill a muscle fiber
Bundles of muscle fibers wrapped in perimysium
questions.why: Myofilaments are the protein strands inside each myofibril. The thick filaments are made mostly of myosin and the thin filaments mostly of actin. Their regular, overlapping arrangement creates the sarcomere, and they are the smallest level in the organization of a skeletal muscle, below the muscle, fascicle, fiber, and myofibril.
notes: This describes the transverse (T) tubules, which carry the surface signal deep into the fiber. They are membrane tunnels, not protein strands.
Correct. Myofilaments are the smallest level of muscle organization, the protein strands whose overlap forms the sarcomere.
This describes myofibrils, one level larger. Each myofibril is built of myofilaments, so pick myofibril if the question asked what fills most of the sarcoplasm.
This describes fascicles, visible bundles of whole cells. A fascicle is several levels above the myofilaments, which are proteins inside a single cell.
questions.answerText: The thick and thin protein strands within a myofibril

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which protein makes up the thick filament?
options: Actin
Titin
Myosin
Tropomyosin
questions.why: The thick filament is built of myosin. Many myosin molecules bundle together, each with a long tail and a pair of heads, and the heads project outward from the filament as cross bridges. Thick filaments lie in the center of the sarcomere, spanning the A band, and are anchored at the M line.
notes: Actin makes up the thin filament, two twisted strands of actin subunits anchored at the Z disc. Pick actin if the question asked about the thin filament.
Titin is a giant structural protein that runs from the Z disc to the M line and gives the sarcomere elastic recoil. It anchors the thick filament but does not form it.
Correct. The thick filament is a bundle of myosin molecules.
Tropomyosin is a rod-shaped regulatory protein lying along the thin filament. Its name contains myosin, which is why students pick it, but it belongs to the thin filament.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Where do the thick filaments lie within the sarcomere?
options: Centered in the A band, joined at the M line
At each end, anchored to the Z disc
Only within the I band
Along the sarcolemma, outside the myofibril
questions.why: Thick filaments sit in the middle of the sarcomere. Their length sets the width of the A band, and their centers are joined at the M line, where myomesin binds them together. Thin filaments reach inward from the Z discs and overlap the ends of the thick filaments, forming the zone of overlap at each edge of the A band.
notes: Correct. The thick filaments define the A band and are tied together at the M line.
This describes the thin filaments, which are anchored at the Z disc and extend inward. Pick this placement if the question asked where the thin filaments attach.
The I band contains thin filaments only, which is why it is light. Thick filaments never extend into the I band.
Thick filaments are inside the myofibril, not on the cell membrane. The protein linking the myofibril to the sarcolemma is dystrophin, which would be the answer for that connection.
questions.answerText: Centered in the A band, joined at the M line

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which protein makes up the thin filament?
options: Myomesin
Actin
Myosin
Dystrophin
questions.why: The thin filament is made mainly of actin. Two strands of actin subunits twist around each other, and each subunit carries a binding site for a myosin head. The thin filament also carries the regulatory proteins tropomyosin and troponin, and it is anchored at the Z disc.
notes: Myomesin is a structural protein at the M line that binds thick filaments together. It is not part of the thin filament, which never reaches the M line.
Correct. The thin filament is two twisted strands of actin subunits.
Myosin forms the thick filament, a bundle of molecules with projecting heads. Pick myosin if the question asked about the thick filament.
Dystrophin links the thin filaments to the sarcolemma, but it does not build the filament itself. It would be the answer for the protein that is faulty in Duchenne muscular dystrophy.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: How far do the thin filaments extend within a sarcomere?
options: From the Z disc partway into the A band
From one Z disc all the way to the next Z disc
Only within the H zone
From the M line to the edge of the A band
questions.why: Each thin filament is anchored at a Z disc and extends inward toward the center of the sarcomere. It crosses the I band, where it is the only filament present, then continues partway into the A band, where it overlaps the thick filaments. It stops before the center, leaving the H zone free of thin filaments.
notes: Correct. The thin filaments reach into the A band to form the zone of overlap, then stop at the H zone.
If thin filaments ran the full sarcomere there would be no H zone, the region of thick filaments only. This option is a misconception that ignores the gap at the center of a relaxed sarcomere.
The H zone is defined as the region containing thick filaments only, so thin filaments are absent there. It is the answer for where thin filaments are missing, not where they lie.
This is roughly the reach of half a thick filament, which is anchored at the M line. Pick this if the question asked where the thick filaments lie.
questions.answerText: From the Z disc partway into the A band

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: Which intermediate filament protein surrounds the Z discs and ties neighboring myofibrils together side by side?
options: Titin
Myomesin
Nebulin
Desmin
questions.why: Desmin is an intermediate filament protein that wraps around the Z discs and connects each myofibril to its neighbors. By tying the myofibrils together at their Z discs, it keeps the sarcomeres of neighboring myofibrils lined up, which is part of why the bands look continuous across the whole fiber. Desmin is not the elastic filament of the sarcomere; that role belongs to titin.
notes: Titin is the elastic filament that runs lengthwise inside each sarcomere, from the Z disc to the M line. Pick titin if the question asked which protein gives the sarcomere elastic recoil.
Myomesin sits at the M line and binds thick filaments together within one sarcomere. It would be the answer for the protein at the center of the sarcomere.
Nebulin runs along the length of the thin filament, anchoring it and setting its length. It works within a single myofibril, not between neighboring ones.
Correct. Desmin links adjacent myofibrils at their Z discs, keeping them in register across the fiber.

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: A myosin molecule is built of how many heavy and light polypeptide chains?
options: Two heavy chains and four light chains
Four heavy chains and two light chains
Two heavy chains and two light chains
One heavy chain and two light chains
questions.why: A myosin molecule has two heavy chains and four light chains. The two heavy chains twist around each other to form the long tail and then each ends in a globular head, so one molecule has a pair of heads. Two light chains are associated with each head, giving four light chains in all.
notes: Correct. The two heavy chains form the tail and heads, and the light chains sit at the heads.
This reverses the numbers. Students who remember both numbers but not which is which choose it. There are two heavy chains, matching the two heads.
This gets the heavy chains right but undercounts the light chains. Each of the two heads carries two light chains, for four in total.
A single heavy chain could not form the paired heads and the intertwined tail of myosin. This choice comes from forgetting that the tail is two chains wound together.
questions.answerText: Two heavy chains and four light chains

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What do the heads of the myosin molecules do in a contracting muscle?
options: They cover the active sites on actin in relaxed muscle
They bind the thin filament as cross bridges and pull on it
They store calcium ions near the myofibrils
They anchor the thick filaments at the M line
questions.why: Each myosin molecule ends in a pair of globular heads that project outward from the thick filament. During contraction these heads attach to binding sites on the actin of the thin filament, forming cross bridges, and they pivot to pull the thin filaments toward the M line. The heads are the force-producing part of the thick filament.
notes: Covering the active sites is the job of tropomyosin, a regulatory protein on the thin filament. It would be the answer if the question asked what blocks cross bridges at rest.
Correct. The heads project from the thick filament and link to actin as cross bridges.
Calcium is stored in the sarcoplasmic reticulum, the smooth endoplasmic reticulum wrapping each myofibril. Pick the sarcoplasmic reticulum for the calcium store.
Anchoring at the M line is done by structural proteins such as myomesin, near the center of the thick filament where there are no heads. Pick myomesin for that role.
questions.answerText: They bind the thin filament as cross bridges and pull on it

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What is the shape of a single myosin molecule?
options: A rod lying end to end along a filament
A small globular complex of three subunits
A long tail with a pair of heads at one end
Two twisted strands of round subunits
questions.why: A myosin molecule has a long tail made of two intertwined heavy chains, and at one end the chains fold into two globular heads, so the molecule looks like two golf clubs twisted together. Hundreds of these molecules bundle tail to tail to build a thick filament, with the heads sticking out to form cross bridges.
notes: This describes tropomyosin, a rod-shaped regulatory protein on the thin filament. It has no heads.
This describes troponin, the three-part regulatory complex bound to tropomyosin. It would be the answer for the protein with TnI, TnT, and TnC subunits.
Correct. The intertwined tail and two heads give myosin its golf club shape.
This describes the thin filament, built from strands of globular actin subunits. Pick it if the question asked about the structure of the thin filament.
questions.answerText: A long tail with a pair of heads at one end

questions.topic: Muscle fiber microanatomy and the sarcomere
questions.q: What does each actin subunit of the thin filament carry?
options: A pair of heads that project outward
A binding site for a myosin head
A link to the sarcolemma
An elastic spring segment
questions.why: The thin filament is built from actin subunits strung in two twisted strands. Each subunit carries an active site, a myosin-binding site where a myosin head can attach to form a cross bridge. In relaxed muscle, the regulatory protein tropomyosin lies over these sites and keeps the heads from binding.
notes: Projecting heads belong to myosin molecules in the thick filament. Pick this if the question asked what forms the cross bridges.
Correct. Each actin subunit has an active site where a myosin head can bind.
The link between the thin filaments and the sarcolemma is made by dystrophin, a separate structural protein. Individual actin subunits do not attach to the membrane.
