Its four tendons pass through the carpal tunnel beneath the tendons of flexor digitorum superficialis, slip through the split in each superficialis tendon, and attach to the base of the distal phalanx of digits 2 to 5. That makes it the only muscle that bends the fingertips at the distal interphalangeal joints.
notes: The middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5 are where flexor digitorum superficialis inserts. Pick this if the question asked about the superficial finger flexor that bends the middle knuckles.
The distal phalanx of the thumb receives flexor pollicis longus, the long thumb flexor. Choose it if the question asked which deep anterior muscle bends the tip of the thumb.
The pisiform, hamate and metacarpal 5 are the insertion of flexor carpi ulnaris on the medial side of the wrist. Pick them if the question asked which muscle flexes and adducts the wrist.
Correct. Flexor digitorum profundus inserts on the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does flexor pollicis longus insert?
options: Distal phalanx of the thumb
Base of metacarpal 2
Base of metacarpal 1
Proximal phalanx of the thumb
questions.why: Flexor pollicis longus arises from the anterior radius and interosseous membrane in the deep layer of the anterior forearm. Its tendon runs through the carpal tunnel to the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb, so it bends the tip of the thumb at the interphalangeal joint. The name gives this away: flexor for the action, pollicis for the thumb, and longus because it is the long thumb flexor that starts in the forearm.
notes: Correct. Flexor pollicis longus inserts on the distal phalanx of the thumb.

The base of metacarpal 2 receives flexor carpi radialis on the palmar side and extensor carpi radialis longus on the dorsal side. Pick it if the question asked about a radial wrist muscle rather than a thumb muscle.

The base of metacarpal 1 is where abductor pollicis longus inserts, on the thumb side of the back of the wrist. Pick it if the question asked which deep posterior forearm muscle moves the thumb away from the palm.

The proximal phalanx of the thumb receives extensor pollicis brevis from the posterior forearm. Choose it if the question asked which muscle extends the thumb at its knuckle (the metacarpophalangeal joint).
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does flexor carpi ulnaris insert?
options: Base of metacarpal 1
Pisiform, hamate and metacarpal 5
Bases of metacarpals 2 and 3
Palmar aponeurosis
questions.why: Flexor carpi ulnaris is the most medial muscle of the superficial anterior forearm. It arises from the medial epicondyle and the olecranon, runs down the ulnar (little finger) side of the forearm, and inserts on the pisiform, the hook of the hamate and the base of metacarpal 5. Pulling on the medial side of the wrist lets it flex the wrist and adduct it toward the little finger side.
notes: The base of metacarpal 1 is the insertion of abductor pollicis longus from the posterior forearm. Choose it if the question asked which muscle abducts the thumb from the forearm.
Correct. Flexor carpi ulnaris inserts on the pisiform, hamate and metacarpal 5.
The bases of metacarpals 2 and 3 receive flexor carpi radialis, the wrist flexor on the thumb side. Pick them if the question named the radial wrist flexor.
The palmar aponeurosis is the insertion of palmaris longus, the slender superficial muscle in the middle of the forearm. Pick it if the question asked which muscle tenses the fascia of the palm.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does flexor carpi radialis do at the wrist?
options: Flexes and adducts the wrist
Extends and adducts the wrist
Extends and abducts the wrist
Flexes and abducts the wrist
questions.why: The name spells out the action. Flexor means it bends the joint, carpi means the wrist, and radialis places it on the radial (thumb) side. Its tendon crosses the front of the wrist on that side and inserts on the bases of metacarpals 2 and 3, so it flexes the wrist and pulls the hand toward the thumb side, which is abduction (also called radial deviation).
notes: Flexing and adducting the wrist is the job of flexor carpi ulnaris, which crosses the wrist on the little finger side. Pick this if the question named the ulnar wrist flexor.
Extending and adducting the wrist is the action of extensor carpi ulnaris, the extensor on the little finger side of the back of the forearm. Pick it if the question named that muscle.
Extending and abducting the wrist is the action of extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis on the back of the forearm. Choose it if the question named a radial wrist extensor.
Correct. Flexor carpi radialis flexes the wrist and abducts it toward the thumb side.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which three muscles make up the deep layer of the anterior forearm?
options: Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus
Supinator, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis longus
Flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus
Flexor digitorum superficialis, flexor carpi ulnaris, pronator teres
questions.why: The deep layer of the anterior forearm lies right against the radius, ulna and interosseous membrane. Flexor digitorum profundus covers the ulnar side, flexor pollicis longus covers the radial side, and pronator quadratus lies under both of them just above the wrist. These deep muscles arise from the bones and the membrane rather than from the medial epicondyle.
notes: Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus are superficial muscles that arise from the medial epicondyle. Pick this group if the question asked which muscles share the common flexor origin.
Supinator, abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis longus belong to the deep layer of the posterior forearm. Choose them if the question asked about deep muscles on the back of the forearm.
Correct. Flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus and pronator quadratus form the deep anterior layer.

None of these three lie against the bones. Flexor digitorum superficialis sits on top of the deep finger flexor, and flexor carpi ulnaris and pronator teres arise from the medial epicondyle, so this group fits a question about muscles lying superficial to flexor digitorum profundus.
questions.answerText: Flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: In a forearm muscle name such as flexor carpi ulnaris, what does the word carpi refer to?
options: The wrist
The forearm
The thumb
The fingers
questions.why: Carpi comes from carpus, the wrist, which is built from the eight carpal bones. Muscles with carpi in their name, such as flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris and the extensor carpi muscles, cross the wrist and insert on carpal or metacarpal bones, so their main job is moving the hand at the wrist rather than moving the fingers.
notes: Correct. Carpi refers to the wrist.

The forearm is the antebrachium, and no muscle in this group uses carpi for it. Students sometimes pick this because the muscle belly sits in the forearm, but carpi names the joint the muscle moves, not where its belly lies.
The thumb is named by pollicis, as in flexor pollicis longus and abductor pollicis longus. Choose it if the name contained pollicis.
The fingers are named by digitorum, as in flexor digitorum superficialis and extensor digitorum. Pick this if the name contained digitorum.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does the word teres in pronator teres describe?
options: A deep position
A round, cylindrical shape
A long length
A square, four-sided shape
questions.why: Teres means round, and it describes the shape of the muscle belly. Pronator teres is a rounded muscle that runs diagonally across the proximal forearm from the medial epicondyle to the lateral radius. Comparing it with pronator quadratus shows how names use shape to tell apart two muscles that have the same action.
notes: Depth is named by profundus, as in flexor digitorum profundus, while superficialis names the shallower muscle. Pick this if the name contained profundus.
Correct. Teres means round and describes the shape of the muscle.
Length is named by longus or brevis, as in flexor pollicis longus or extensor carpi radialis brevis. Choose it if the name contained one of those words.
Square or four-sided is quadratus, as in pronator quadratus in the distal forearm. Pick this if the name contained quadratus.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: From which two sites does pronator teres originate?
options: Lateral epicondyle and proximal ulna
Medial epicondyle and olecranon
Anterior radius and interosseous membrane
Medial epicondyle and coronoid process of the ulna
questions.why: Pronator teres has two heads. The larger head comes from the medial epicondyle as part of the common flexor origin, and a smaller head comes from the coronoid process of the ulna. Both heads join and run diagonally to the lateral mid-shaft of the radius, which is why the muscle pronates the forearm.
notes: The lateral epicondyle and proximal ulna are the origins of supinator, the deep posterior muscle that does the opposite movement. Choose it if the question asked where supinator arises.
The medial epicondyle and olecranon are the origins of flexor carpi ulnaris, the most medial superficial flexor. Pick this if the question named flexor carpi ulnaris.
The anterior radius and interosseous membrane give origin to flexor pollicis longus in the deep anterior layer. Pick this if the question asked where the long thumb flexor begins.
Correct. Pronator teres arises from the medial epicondyle and the coronoid process of the ulna.
questions.answerText: Medial epicondyle and coronoid process of the ulna
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does flexor pollicis longus originate?
options: Anterior and medial ulna and interosseous membrane
Distal anterior ulna
Anterior radius and interosseous membrane
Medial epicondyle of the humerus
questions.why: Flexor pollicis longus is a deep anterior forearm muscle that lies on the radial (thumb) side. It arises from the anterior surface of the radius and the neighboring interosseous membrane, the sheet of dense connective tissue that joins the radius and ulna. Starting on the radius lines it up with the thumb, which it flexes.
notes: The anterior and medial ulna and interosseous membrane are the origin of flexor digitorum profundus, the deep flexor beside it on the ulnar side. Pick this if the question asked where the deep finger flexor begins.
The distal anterior ulna is the origin of pronator quadratus, the square muscle just above the wrist. Pick it if the question asked where pronator quadratus begins.
Correct. Flexor pollicis longus arises from the anterior radius and interosseous membrane.
The medial epicondyle is the common flexor origin used by the superficial muscles such as flexor carpi radialis. Choose it if the question asked about a superficial anterior forearm muscle.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What is the main action of palmaris longus?
options: Flexes the thumb at its tip
Abducts the wrist toward the thumb
Pronates the forearm at the radioulnar joints
Tenses the palmar aponeurosis
questions.why: Palmaris longus has a slender tendon that runs down the middle of the wrist and fans out into the palmar aponeurosis. When it contracts it pulls that sheet tight and gives a weak assist to wrist flexion. It is a small muscle that many people lack on one or both sides, and its absence causes no noticeable weakness because the other wrist flexors do the work.
notes: Flexing the thumb is the job of flexor pollicis longus in the deep layer, along with the short thumb flexor in the hand. Choose this if the question named a muscle with pollicis in its name.

Abducting the wrist is done by flexor carpi radialis working with the radial wrist extensors on the thumb side. Palmaris longus runs down the middle of the wrist, so it does not tilt the hand to either side.
Pronation is done by pronator teres and pronator quadratus, which pull the radius across the ulna. Pick this if the question named one of the pronators.
Correct. Palmaris longus tenses the palmar aponeurosis and weakly assists wrist flexion.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does flexor digitorum profundus originate?
options: Anterior radius and interosseous membrane
Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
Anterior and medial ulna and interosseous membrane
Medial epicondyle, coronoid process and radius
questions.why: Flexor digitorum profundus is the deep finger flexor, so it does not reach up to the medial epicondyle. It arises from the anterior and medial surfaces of the ulna and the interosseous membrane, lying on the ulnar side of the deep layer next to flexor pollicis longus. From there its four tendons run to the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5.
notes: The anterior radius and interosseous membrane give origin to flexor pollicis longus, the deep muscle on the thumb side. Choose it if the question asked about the long thumb flexor.
The lateral epicondyle is the common extensor origin for the superficial posterior muscles, such as extensor digitorum. Pick it if the question asked where the finger extensor begins.
Correct. Flexor digitorum profundus arises from the anterior and medial ulna and the interosseous membrane.

The medial epicondyle, coronoid process and radius are the origins of flexor digitorum superficialis, the finger flexor that lies on top. Pick this if the question asked where the superficial finger flexor begins.
questions.answerText: Anterior and medial ulna and interosseous membrane
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: In flexor digitorum superficialis, what does superficialis tell you about the muscle?
options: It is the stronger of the two finger flexors
It is the shorter of the two finger flexors
It lies closer to the surface than its partner
It lies on the radial side of the forearm
questions.why: Superficialis means nearer the surface. Flexor digitorum superficialis lies on top of flexor digitorum profundus, whose name means deep. The two muscles share the same action on the same fingers, so their names separate them by depth, and their insertions follow the same logic: the superficial one stops at the middle phalanges and the deep one reaches the distal phalanges.
notes: Names rarely describe strength, and superficialis says nothing about force. Students choose this when they read superficial as dominant, but the word only places the muscle closer to the skin.
Relative length is named by brevis or longus, as in extensor carpi radialis brevis and longus. Choose this if the name contained brevis.
Correct. Superficialis means the muscle lies superficial to flexor digitorum profundus.
The side of the forearm is named by radialis or ulnaris, as in flexor carpi radialis. Pick this if the name contained radialis.
questions.answerText: It lies closer to the surface than its partner
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What are the origin and insertion of brachioradialis?
options: Medial epicondyle to the lateral mid-shaft of the radius
Lateral supracondylar ridge to the styloid process of the radius
Lateral epicondyle to the proximal lateral radius
Lateral epicondyle to the base of metacarpal 3
questions.why: Brachioradialis begins on the lateral supracondylar ridge, the sharp edge of the humerus just above the lateral epicondyle, and runs down the thumb side of the forearm to the styloid process of the radius. Its name joins brachio (arm) and radialis (radius), which matches a muscle that spans from the arm to the distal radius. It forms the fleshy lateral edge of the forearm you can feel just below the elbow.
notes: Medial epicondyle to the lateral mid-shaft of the radius describes pronator teres. Pick this if the question asked for the attachments of the round pronator.
Correct. Brachioradialis runs from the lateral supracondylar ridge to the styloid process of the radius.
Lateral epicondyle to the proximal lateral radius describes supinator, which wraps around the upper radius. Pick it if the question asked which muscle supinates the forearm.
Lateral epicondyle to the base of metacarpal 3 describes extensor carpi radialis brevis. Choose it if the question asked about the shorter radial wrist extensor.
questions.answerText: Lateral supracondylar ridge to the styloid process of the radius
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which list gives the superficial anterior forearm muscles in order from lateral (thumb side) to medial (little finger side)?
options: Flexor carpi radialis, pronator teres, flexor carpi ulnaris, palmaris longus
Pronator teres, palmaris longus, flexor carpi radialis, flexor carpi ulnaris
Flexor carpi ulnaris, palmaris longus, flexor carpi radialis, pronator teres
Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: All four muscles fan out from the medial epicondyle, but they end up side by side across the front of the forearm. Pronator teres is the most lateral because it heads for the radius, flexor carpi radialis lies next to it on the thumb side, palmaris longus runs down the middle, and flexor carpi ulnaris is the most medial on the little finger side. The words radialis and ulnaris in two of the names confirm which side each belongs on.
notes: This list swaps two pairs of neighbors. Flexor carpi radialis lies medial to pronator teres, not lateral to it, and palmaris longus sits between the two carpi muscles in the middle of the forearm rather than at the medial edge.
This list puts palmaris longus on the thumb side of flexor carpi radialis. Palmaris longus actually runs down the middle of the forearm, between flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris.
This is the correct sequence written backward, from medial to lateral. Pick it if the question asked for the order starting on the little finger side.
Correct. From lateral to medial the order is pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris.
questions.answerText: Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Why is flexor digitorum profundus the only muscle that can bend the fingertips of digits 2 to 5 at the distal interphalangeal joints?
options: It is the only finger flexor that lies in the superficial layer
It is the only finger flexor that inserts on the distal phalanges
It is the only finger flexor that passes through the carpal tunnel
It is the only finger flexor that arises from the medial epicondyle
questions.why: A muscle can only move the joints its tendon crosses. Flexor digitorum profundus is the only muscle whose tendons reach the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5, so it is the only one that crosses and flexes the distal interphalangeal joints. Flexor digitorum superficialis stops at the middle phalanges, so it can bend the middle knuckles but not the fingertips.
notes: Profundus means deep, and the muscle lies in the deep layer beneath flexor digitorum superficialis. This choice reverses the meaning of its name.
Correct. Only profundus reaches the distal phalanges of digits 2 to 5.

Flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor pollicis longus also pass through the carpal tunnel, so this does not set profundus apart. This idea fits a question about why swelling in the tunnel can affect all the long flexor tendons at once.

Profundus arises from the ulna and interosseous membrane, not the medial epicondyle. Flexor digitorum superficialis is the finger flexor with a medial epicondyle origin, so pick this kind of answer for a question about superficialis.
questions.answerText: It is the only finger flexor that inserts on the distal phalanges
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Flexor digitorum superficialis lies on top of flexor digitorum profundus, yet the deep muscle's tendons reach farther out in each finger. How does the profundus tendon get past the superficialis tendon?
options: The profundus tendon loops around the outer side of the proximal phalanx
The superficialis tendon splits and the profundus tendon passes through the gap
The profundus tendon runs along the back of the finger to reach the tip
The superficialis tendon ends at the wrist, well before reaching the fingers
questions.why: Near the base of each finger, the superficialis tendon divides into two slips that pass around the profundus tendon and attach to the sides of the middle phalanx. The profundus tendon slides through this split and continues on to the distal phalanx. This arrangement lets two stacked muscles share the same fingers while each one controls a different joint.
notes: Both long flexor tendons stay together on the palmar side of the finger. They do not detour around the bone, so this choice comes from guessing how two tendons might avoid each other rather than from the actual anatomy.
Correct. The superficialis tendon splits so the profundus tendon can pass through to the distal phalanx.

The back of the finger carries the extensor expansion, which receives the extensor digitorum tendon. A tendon on the back of the finger would straighten it, so pick this only if the question asked how the extensor tendons reach the fingers.
Superficialis does reach the fingers and inserts on the middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5. A muscle that ended at the wrist would act only on the wrist, like flexor carpi radialis.
questions.answerText: The superficialis tendon splits and the profundus tendon passes through the gap
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor digitorum profundus?
options: Both insert on the distal phalanges and differ only in where they arise
Superficialis inserts on the distal phalanges, and profundus inserts on the middle phalanges
Superficialis acts on the thumb, and profundus acts on digits 2 to 5
Superficialis inserts on the middle phalanges, and profundus inserts on the distal phalanges
questions.why: Both muscles flex digits 2 to 5, but they are stacked in two layers and reach different bones. Superficialis lies on top and stops at the middle phalanges, so it bends the proximal interphalangeal joints. Profundus lies deeper and reaches the distal phalanges, so it is the muscle that bends the fingertips. The deeper muscle is the one that reaches farther.
notes: They do differ in origin, but they also differ in insertion. If both reached the distal phalanges, a clinician could not test them separately by asking the patient to bend one joint at a time.
This reverses the two insertions. It would be correct only if the names were swapped, so remember that the deep muscle reaches the more distal bone.
Neither muscle acts on the thumb. The long thumb flexor is flexor pollicis longus, so pick a statement about the thumb only if it named that muscle.
Correct. Superficialis ends on the middle phalanges and profundus on the distal phalanges.
questions.answerText: Superficialis inserts on the middle phalanges, and profundus inserts on the distal phalanges
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which pair of muscles works together to abduct the wrist, tilting the hand toward the thumb side?
options: Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris
Extensor carpi radialis longus and extensor carpi ulnaris
Flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis longus
Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: Abduction of the wrist (radial deviation) needs muscles on the thumb side of the wrist. Flexor carpi radialis crosses the front of the wrist on that side and extensor carpi radialis longus crosses the back. Each one alone would also flex or extend, but when they contract together the flexion and extension cancel out and the hand tilts straight toward the thumb.
notes: Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris both cross the front of the wrist, one on each side, so together they flex the wrist straight forward while their side-to-side pulls cancel. Choose them for a question about pure wrist flexion.

Extensor carpi radialis longus and extensor carpi ulnaris both cross the back of the wrist, one on each side, so together they extend the wrist straight back. Pick them for a question about pure wrist extension.
Correct. These two radial muscles, one flexor and one extensor, combine to abduct the wrist.

Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris both cross the wrist on the little finger side, so together they adduct the wrist. Pick this pair if the question asked about tilting the hand toward the little finger.
questions.answerText: Flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis longus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares pronator teres and pronator quadratus?
options: Pronator teres runs straight across the distal forearm, and pronator quadratus runs diagonally near the elbow
Pronator teres runs diagonally near the elbow, and pronator quadratus runs straight across the distal forearm
Pronator teres lies in the deep layer, and pronator quadratus lies in the superficial layer
Pronator teres supinates the forearm, and pronator quadratus pronates it
questions.why: Both muscles pronate the forearm by pulling the radius across the ulna, but they sit at opposite ends of the forearm and have different shapes. Pronator teres is a round muscle that runs diagonally from the medial epicondyle and coronoid process to the lateral mid-shaft of the radius. Pronator quadratus is a flat, square muscle that runs horizontally between the distal ulna and distal radius, deep to the flexor tendons.
notes: This swaps the positions of the two muscles. The square muscle (quadratus) is the horizontal one at the wrist end, and the round one (teres) is the diagonal one near the elbow.
Correct. Teres is the diagonal, round pronator near the elbow, and quadratus is the square pronator just above the wrist.
This reverses the layers. Pronator teres is a superficial muscle from the medial epicondyle, while pronator quadratus is in the deep layer lying directly on the bones.
Both muscles pronate, as their names say. Supination belongs to supinator and biceps brachii, so pick a statement about supination only if it named one of those.
questions.answerText: Pronator teres runs diagonally near the elbow, and pronator quadratus runs straight across the distal forearm
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Besides pronating the forearm, pronator teres also assists which movement, because it crosses the front of the elbow?
options: Forearm supination
Wrist flexion
Elbow extension
Elbow flexion
questions.why: A muscle acts on every joint it crosses, and the side it crosses on decides the movement. Pronator teres arises above the elbow on the medial epicondyle and inserts below it on the radius, crossing the anterior side of the elbow. Pulling across the front of a hinge joint bends it, so the muscle gives a small assist to elbow flexion along with its main job of pronation.
notes: Supination is the opposite of pronation and is done by supinator and biceps brachii. A muscle cannot both pronate and supinate, so pick this if the question asked about supinator.
Pronator teres ends on the mid-shaft of the radius and never crosses the wrist, so it cannot move the wrist. Choose wrist flexion for muscles such as flexor carpi radialis that reach the hand.
Elbow extension needs a muscle crossing the back of the elbow, like triceps brachii inserting on the olecranon. Pick this if the question described a posterior muscle.
Correct. Crossing the front of the elbow lets pronator teres assist elbow flexion.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris both flex the wrist. Why does one abduct the wrist while the other adducts it?
options: Their tendons cross the wrist on opposite sides
They arise from different epicondyles of the humerus
One inserts on the fingers and the other on the carpal bones
One lies in the superficial layer and the other in the deep layer
questions.why: Side-to-side movement at the wrist depends on which side of the wrist a tendon crosses. Flexor carpi radialis crosses on the radial (thumb) side and inserts on metacarpals 2 and 3, so it tilts the hand toward the thumb, which is abduction. Flexor carpi ulnaris crosses on the ulnar (little finger) side and inserts on the pisiform, hamate and metacarpal 5, so it tilts the hand toward the little finger, which is adduction.
notes: Correct. The side of the wrist each tendon crosses decides whether it abducts or adducts.

Both muscles arise from the medial epicondyle as part of the common flexor origin, so origin cannot explain the difference. Different epicondyles would explain why a flexor and an extensor differ, not two flexors.
Neither inserts on the fingers. Both insert on carpal and metacarpal bones, which is why their names contain carpi rather than digitorum.

Both are superficial muscles of the anterior forearm. Layer explains why flexor digitorum profundus differs from flexor digitorum superficialis, not why these two tilt the wrist in opposite directions.
questions.answerText: Their tendons cross the wrist on opposite sides
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A muscle arises from the anterior radius and interosseous membrane and inserts on the distal phalanx of the thumb. Which muscle is it?
options: Abductor pollicis longus
Flexor pollicis longus
Flexor pollicis brevis
Extensor pollicis longus
questions.why: Starting on the anterior radius places this muscle in the deep layer of the anterior forearm, so it is a flexor, and reaching the distal phalanx of the thumb means it bends the thumb tip. That matches flexor pollicis longus. The word longus tells you it is the long thumb flexor that starts in the forearm, unlike the short thumb flexor that lives in the hand.
notes: Abductor pollicis longus arises from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane and inserts on the base of metacarpal 1. Pick it if the question asked which posterior muscle moves the thumb away from the palm.
Correct. Flexor pollicis longus runs from the anterior radius and interosseous membrane to the distal phalanx of the thumb.

Flexor pollicis brevis is a short thenar muscle that lies entirely in the hand at the base of the thumb. It cannot arise from the radius, so pick it if the question asked about an intrinsic thenar muscle.

Extensor pollicis longus also reaches the distal phalanx of the thumb, but it arises from the posterior ulna and interosseous membrane and runs on the back of the wrist. Choose it if the question asked which muscle straightens the tip of the thumb.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which two anterior forearm muscles arise partly from the interosseous membrane between the radius and ulna?
options: Flexor digitorum profundus and flexor pollicis longus
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
Pronator teres and flexor carpi radialis
Palmaris longus and flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: The interosseous membrane is a sheet of dense connective tissue that spans the gap between the radius and ulna, and deep forearm muscles use it as extra attachment surface. In the anterior forearm, flexor digitorum profundus arises from the ulna and the membrane, and flexor pollicis longus arises from the radius and the membrane, so both lie directly on it.
notes: Correct. Both deep finger and thumb flexors arise partly from the interosseous membrane.
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus both come from the medial epicondyle as part of the common flexor origin. The deeper finger flexors separate them from the membrane.

Pronator teres and flexor carpi radialis arise from the medial epicondyle, and pronator teres also from the coronoid process. They are superficial and do not reach the membrane, so choose them for a question about the common flexor origin.

Palmaris longus and flexor carpi ulnaris are superficial muscles from the medial epicondyle, with flexor carpi ulnaris also arising from the olecranon. Pick them if the question asked about superficial flexors on the medial side.
questions.answerText: Flexor digitorum profundus and flexor pollicis longus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: When a person touches the tips of the thumb and little finger together and slightly flexes the wrist, a thin tendon often stands out in the middle of the front of the wrist. Which muscle does it belong to?
options: Palmaris longus
Flexor pollicis longus
Flexor carpi radialis
Flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: Palmaris longus has a slender tendon that runs down the center of the anterior wrist and passes in front of the flexor retinaculum into the palmar aponeurosis. Cupping the palm and flexing the wrist tightens it, so it stands out in the midline. Because the muscle is absent in many people, some will see no tendon in this spot even though their other flexors are normal.
notes: Correct. The thin midline tendon belongs to palmaris longus.
Flexor pollicis longus lies in the deep layer and its tendon passes through the carpal tunnel, so it does not stand out under the skin. Pick it if the question asked which tendon bends the thumb tip.
Flexor carpi radialis has a thicker tendon just to the thumb side of the midline. Choose it if the question described the tendon used as a landmark for the radial pulse.
Flexor carpi ulnaris has its tendon at the medial (little finger) edge of the wrist, heading to the pisiform. Pick it if the question described the tendon at the ulnar edge.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: To take a radial pulse, you press on the radial artery where it lies directly lateral to a prominent tendon at the front of the wrist. Which muscle does that tendon belong to?
options: Flexor digitorum superficialis
Flexor carpi radialis
Palmaris longus
Flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: At the wrist the radial artery runs on the thumb side between the tendon of flexor carpi radialis and the distal radius. Pressing just lateral to that tendon pushes the artery against the bone, which is why the pulse is easy to feel there. The tendon makes a reliable landmark because it stands out when the wrist is flexed against resistance.
notes: The flexor digitorum superficialis tendons lie deeper and closer to the middle of the wrist and pass through the carpal tunnel, so they are not the palpable landmark for the radial pulse.
Correct. The radial pulse is felt just lateral to the flexor carpi radialis tendon.

Palmaris longus runs down the midline of the wrist, medial to flexor carpi radialis, so the radial artery is not directly beside it. Pick it if the question asked about the thin tendon in the center of the wrist.
Flexor carpi ulnaris lies on the little finger side of the wrist, and the ulnar artery runs just lateral to its tendon. Choose it if the question asked where to feel the ulnar pulse.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which superficial anterior forearm muscle does not cross the wrist?
options: Flexor carpi radialis
Palmaris longus
Flexor carpi ulnaris
Pronator teres
questions.why: Pronator teres inserts on the lateral mid-shaft of the radius, partway down the forearm, so it never reaches the wrist. That is why it acts only at the forearm and elbow, pronating the forearm and assisting elbow flexion. The other superficial muscles from the medial epicondyle all send tendons across the wrist to the hand.
notes: Flexor carpi radialis crosses the front of the wrist on the thumb side to reach metacarpals 2 and 3. Pick it if the question asked which superficial flexor abducts the wrist.
Palmaris longus crosses the middle of the wrist to reach the palmar aponeurosis. Choose it if the question asked which muscle tenses the fascia of the palm.
Flexor carpi ulnaris crosses the wrist on the little finger side to reach the pisiform, hamate and metacarpal 5. Pick it if the question asked which superficial flexor adducts the wrist.
Correct. Pronator teres stops on the mid-shaft of the radius and does not cross the wrist.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Brachioradialis crosses the front of the elbow but does not cross the wrist. Which action does it produce?
options: Extends the elbow along with triceps brachii
Extends the wrist and abducts the hand toward the thumb
Flexes the elbow, most strongly with the forearm in mid-position
Flexes the wrist and adducts the hand toward the little finger
questions.why: Brachioradialis runs from the lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus to the styloid process of the radius, so the only joint it crosses is the elbow, and it crosses on the anterior side. That makes it an elbow flexor. The course notes point out that it pulls hardest with the forearm in mid-position, halfway between pronation and supination, as when you lift a mug by its handle with the thumb up.
notes: Elbow extension comes from muscles crossing the back of the elbow, such as triceps brachii inserting on the olecranon. Pick this if the question asked about the posterior arm.
Extending and abducting the wrist is done by extensor carpi radialis longus, which crosses the wrist to metacarpal 2. Brachioradialis stops on the radius and cannot move the wrist.
Correct. Brachioradialis flexes the elbow and is strongest with the forearm in mid-position.
Flexing and adducting the wrist is the action of flexor carpi ulnaris, which crosses the wrist on the little finger side. Brachioradialis does not reach the hand.
questions.answerText: Flexes the elbow, most strongly with the forearm in mid-position
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: After a knife cut across the palm side of a finger, a patient can bend the middle knuckle of that finger but cannot bend the fingertip, even when the other fingers are held straight. Which tendon was most likely cut?
options: Flexor digitorum superficialis
Flexor digitorum profundus
Extensor digitorum
Flexor pollicis longus
questions.why: Bending the fingertip happens at the distal interphalangeal joint, and the only muscle that reaches the distal phalanx of digits 2 to 5 is flexor digitorum profundus. The patient can still bend the middle knuckle because flexor digitorum superficialis, which inserts on the middle phalanx, is intact. Losing only the fingertip movement points to a cut profundus tendon beyond the point where superficialis attaches.
notes: If the superficialis tendon were cut, the patient would be unable to bend the middle knuckle when the other fingers were held straight. Pick it if the scenario described loss of middle knuckle flexion with the fingertip still working.
Correct. Only the profundus tendon bends the fingertip, so its loss explains this finding.
Extensor digitorum runs on the back of the hand and straightens the fingers. A cut extensor tendon would leave the finger unable to straighten, so choose it if the cut were on the back of the finger.
Flexor pollicis longus bends the tip of the thumb, not the fingers. Pick it if the patient could not bend the tip of the thumb.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A patient can bend the thumb at its knuckle but cannot bend the tip of the thumb. Which muscle's tendon is most likely damaged?
options: Extensor pollicis longus
Flexor pollicis longus
Abductor pollicis longus
Flexor pollicis brevis
questions.why: The tip of the thumb bends at the interphalangeal joint, and the only muscle that inserts on the palmar side of the distal phalanx of the thumb is flexor pollicis longus. The knuckle (metacarpophalangeal joint) can still bend because flexor pollicis brevis, a short thenar muscle in the hand, inserts on the proximal phalanx and crosses that joint. Losing tip flexion alone points to the long flexor.
notes: Extensor pollicis longus straightens the tip of the thumb from the back of the hand. Damage to it would leave the thumb tip unable to straighten, so choose it for that scenario.
Correct. Flexor pollicis longus is the only muscle that bends the thumb tip.
Abductor pollicis longus inserts on the base of metacarpal 1 and moves the thumb away from the palm. Pick it if the patient could not pull the thumb away from the hand.

Flexor pollicis brevis is the short thenar muscle that bends the thumb at its knuckle, and its working is why the knuckle still bends here. Pick it if the question asked which thenar muscle flexes the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A golfer has pain at the medial epicondyle that gets worse when he flexes his wrist against resistance. Which structure is most likely irritated?
options: The triceps brachii tendon at the olecranon
The biceps brachii tendon at the radial tuberosity
The common extensor tendon at the lateral epicondyle
The common flexor tendon at the medial epicondyle
questions.why: Golfer's elbow (medial epicondylitis) is irritation of the shared tendon where the superficial anterior forearm muscles attach to the medial epicondyle. Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus and flexor carpi ulnaris all pull on that one spot, so resisted wrist flexion loads the sore tendon and reproduces the pain. Knowing the common flexor origin lets you predict which movements will hurt.
notes: The triceps tendon inserts on the olecranon at the back of the elbow. Irritation there would hurt with resisted elbow extension, so choose it for posterior elbow pain.
The biceps tendon inserts on the radial tuberosity at the front of the elbow. Irritation there would hurt with resisted elbow flexion and supination, so pick it for pain in the front of the elbow.
The common extensor tendon on the lateral epicondyle is the site of tennis elbow, which hurts on the outer elbow with resisted wrist extension. Pick it if the pain were lateral.
Correct. Medial elbow pain with resisted wrist flexion points to the common flexor origin.
questions.answerText: The common flexor tendon at the medial epicondyle
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A person pours water from a pitcher by turning the palm from facing up to facing down while keeping the elbow straight. Which two muscles produce this movement?
options: Brachialis and brachioradialis
Supinator and biceps brachii
Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris
Pronator teres and pronator quadratus
questions.why: Turning the palm from facing up to facing down is pronation, in which the radius rolls across the front of the ulna. Pronator teres and pronator quadratus both pull the radius toward the ulna to make that happen, with pronator quadratus as the prime mover. Keeping the elbow straight rules out the elbow flexors and leaves rotation of the forearm as the only movement.
notes: Brachialis and brachioradialis flex the elbow. Pick them if the person were lifting the pitcher toward the body by bending the elbow.
Supinator and biceps brachii turn the palm the other way, from facing down to facing up. Pick them if the person were turning the hand over to catch water in the palm.
Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris bend the wrist forward together. Choose them if the person tipped the pitcher by bending the wrist instead of rotating the forearm.
Correct. Pronator teres and pronator quadratus pronate the forearm.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A surgeon removes the palmaris longus tendon to use as a graft for repairing a tendon elsewhere. Why does the patient have little or no loss of hand function afterward?
options: Its job is minor, and stronger wrist flexors take over
Palmaris longus mainly pronates the forearm, and pronator quadratus takes over
Palmaris longus regrows within a few weeks
Palmaris longus only acts on the thumb, which has other muscles
questions.why: Palmaris longus is a small muscle whose main job is tightening the palmar aponeurosis, with only a weak assist to wrist flexion. Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris are much stronger wrist flexors and cover that movement completely. This is also why many people born without palmaris longus never notice it is missing, and why its long, thin tendon makes a convenient graft.
notes: Correct. Its action is minor and the other wrist flexors are much stronger.
Palmaris longus does not pronate the forearm. Pronation belongs to pronator teres and pronator quadratus, so this choice fits a question about losing one of the pronators.
A removed tendon does not regrow into a working muscle. This choice comes from assuming the body simply replaces the tissue, when the real reason is that other muscles already cover its job.
Palmaris longus does not reach the thumb. It ends in the palmar aponeurosis in the center of the palm, so a thumb-related answer would fit a muscle like flexor pollicis longus instead.
questions.answerText: Its job is minor, and stronger wrist flexors take over
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: When a patient flexes the wrist, the hand drifts toward the thumb side instead of bending straight forward. Weakness of which muscle best explains this?
options: Palmaris longus
Flexor carpi radialis
Flexor carpi ulnaris
Extensor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: Straight wrist flexion depends on balanced pull from flexor carpi radialis on the thumb side and flexor carpi ulnaris on the little finger side. If flexor carpi ulnaris is weak, the radial flexor's pull is unopposed, so the hand both flexes and abducts toward the thumb. Thinking of each muscle as a pull on one corner of the wrist lets you predict the drift.
notes: Palmaris longus pulls down the middle of the wrist and is only a weak flexor, so losing it does not tilt the hand to either side. Many people lack it with no change in wrist movement.
Weak flexor carpi radialis would leave flexor carpi ulnaris unopposed, so the hand would drift toward the little finger side during flexion. Pick it if the scenario described that ulnar drift.
Correct. Without flexor carpi ulnaris, the radial flexor pulls the flexing hand toward the thumb.
Extensor carpi ulnaris is on the back of the forearm and extends the wrist, so it does not take part in wrist flexion. Choose it if the hand drifted toward the thumb during wrist extension.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A climber grips a hold tightly, curling all four fingers fully at both the middle knuckles and the fingertips. Which two forearm muscles provide this finger flexion?
options: Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris
Pronator teres and pronator quadratus
Extensor digitorum and extensor indicis
Flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor digitorum profundus
questions.why: Curling the fingers at the middle knuckles and fingertips needs muscles that reach the middle and distal phalanges. Flexor digitorum superficialis inserts on the middle phalanges and flexes the proximal interphalangeal joints, and flexor digitorum profundus inserts on the distal phalanges and flexes the distal interphalangeal joints. Both also help flex the knuckles and wrist because their tendons cross those joints on the way.
notes: Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris insert on wrist and metacarpal bones, as carpi in their names says, so they bend the wrist but not the fingers. Pick them if the climber were bending the wrist.
Pronator teres and pronator quadratus rotate the forearm to turn the palm down. Choose them if the climber were rotating the forearm rather than curling the fingers.
Extensor digitorum and extensor indicis straighten the fingers, which is what the climber does to let go of the hold. Pick them for releasing a grip.
Correct. The two long finger flexors curl the fingers at both interphalangeal joints.
questions.answerText: Flexor digitorum superficialis and flexor digitorum profundus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A muscle arises from the medial epicondyle and runs diagonally across the front of the forearm to attach on the lateral side of the radius. Without knowing its name, which action would you predict?
options: Pronation of the forearm
Extension of the wrist
Supination of the forearm
Extension of the elbow
questions.why: Pulling the lateral side of the radius toward the medial side of the elbow rolls the radius across the front of the ulna, and that rotation turns the palm to face posteriorly, which is pronation. The muscle also crosses the front of the elbow, which fits an anterior compartment muscle rather than an extensor. These are the attachments of pronator teres, so reasoning from origin and insertion leads straight to its name.
notes: Correct. These attachments pull the radius across the ulna and pronate the forearm.
Wrist extension needs a muscle that crosses the back of the wrist. This muscle stops on the radius, so it cannot move the wrist at all.
Supination is the opposite rotation, produced by supinator, which wraps around the proximal radius from the lateral epicondyle and ulna. Pick it if the attachments described that wrap from the back.
Elbow extension needs a muscle that crosses the back of the elbow, such as triceps brachii inserting on the olecranon. Choose it if the muscle ran down the back of the arm.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What is the general action of the muscles in the posterior compartment of the forearm?
options: Flexing the wrist and fingers and pronating the forearm
Flexing the elbow and supinating the forearm
Extending the wrist and fingers and supinating the forearm
Extending the elbow and the shoulder
questions.why: The posterior forearm compartment holds the extensors and the supinator. Most of its superficial muscles share a common origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and extend the wrist and fingers, and the deep supinator turns the palm up. This is the mirror image of the anterior compartment, which flexes and pronates.
notes: Flexing the wrist and fingers and pronating the forearm is the job of the anterior forearm compartment. Pick this if the question asked about the muscles that share the medial epicondyle origin.
Flexing the elbow and supinating the forearm is the job of biceps brachii in the anterior arm. Students pick it because supination appears in both answers.
Correct. The posterior forearm extends the wrist and fingers and supinates the forearm.
Extending the elbow and shoulder is done by the triceps brachii in the posterior arm, along with muscles such as latissimus dorsi. It would be the answer for the posterior arm, not the forearm.
questions.answerText: Extending the wrist and fingers and supinating the forearm
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Based on its name, in which forearm compartment does extensor carpi ulnaris lie, and what does it do?
options: Posterior compartment; extends and adducts the wrist
Posterior compartment; extends and abducts the wrist
Anterior compartment; flexes and adducts the wrist
Anterior compartment; flexes and abducts the wrist
questions.why: Extensor tells you the action and places the muscle in the posterior (extensor) compartment. Carpi means the wrist, and ulnaris means the ulnar (little finger) side, so the muscle extends the wrist while pulling it toward the ulnar side, which is adduction of the wrist. It arises from the lateral epicondyle and posterior ulna and inserts on the base of metacarpal 5.
notes: Correct. Extensor carpi ulnaris is a posterior compartment muscle that extends and adducts the wrist.
Extending and abducting the wrist is the action of extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis, on the radial (thumb) side. It would be the answer for a muscle named radialis.
Flexing and adducting the wrist is the action of flexor carpi ulnaris, its anterior partner on the same side. Pick this if the muscle's name began with flexor.
Flexing and abducting the wrist is the action of flexor carpi radialis in the anterior compartment. Choose this for a muscle named flexor carpi radialis.
questions.answerText: Posterior compartment; extends and adducts the wrist
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A tennis player develops pain on the outer side of the elbow after many backhand strokes. This tennis elbow is inflammation at which site?
options: The lateral epicondyle, the common extensor origin
The medial epicondyle, the common flexor origin
The olecranon, where the triceps brachii inserts
The radial tuberosity, where the biceps brachii inserts
questions.why: Most of the superficial muscles of the posterior forearm, the wrist and finger extensors, share a common origin on the lateral epicondyle of the humerus. Repeated forceful wrist extension, as in a backhand stroke, strains that shared attachment and inflames it. Golfer's elbow is the same problem on the opposite side, at the common flexor origin on the medial epicondyle.
notes: Correct. Tennis elbow affects the common extensor origin on the lateral epicondyle.
The medial epicondyle is the common origin of the superficial forearm flexors, and inflammation there is golfer's elbow. Pick it if the pain were on the inner side of the elbow.
The olecranon is the point of the elbow where the triceps brachii attaches to extend the elbow. It would be the answer if the question asked where the triceps inserts.

The radial tuberosity is just below the elbow on the radius, where the biceps brachii inserts to flex the elbow and supinate the forearm. Choose it if the question asked where the biceps tendon attaches.
questions.answerText: The lateral epicondyle, the common extensor origin
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Most superficial posterior forearm muscles share one common extensor origin. Which bony landmark is it?
options: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
Olecranon of the ulna
Medial epicondyle of the humerus
questions.why: The lateral epicondyle is the knob on the lateral side of the distal humerus, and it is the common extensor origin. Extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi and extensor carpi ulnaris all arise there from a shared tendon. Irritation of that tendon is called tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis).
notes: The lateral supracondylar ridge is the sharp edge just above the lateral epicondyle. Extensor carpi radialis longus and brachioradialis arise there, so choose it if the question named one of those two muscles.
Correct. The lateral epicondyle is the common extensor origin.
The olecranon is the point of the elbow on the ulna, where triceps brachii inserts. Pick it if the question asked for the insertion of triceps brachii.
The medial epicondyle is the common flexor origin for the superficial anterior forearm muscles. Pick it if the question asked where the wrist and finger flexors begin.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does extensor carpi radialis longus originate?
options: Lateral epicondyle of the humerus
Medial epicondyle of the humerus
Posterior ulna and interosseous membrane
Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
questions.why: Extensor carpi radialis longus is the one radial wrist extensor that starts above the common extensor origin. It arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge, the edge of the humerus just above the lateral epicondyle, and runs down the thumb side of the back of the forearm to the base of metacarpal 2. Its higher starting point is part of why it is longer than extensor carpi radialis brevis.
notes: The lateral epicondyle is the origin of extensor carpi radialis brevis and the other common extensors. Pick it if the question asked about the shorter radial wrist extensor.
The medial epicondyle is the common flexor origin on the opposite side of the elbow. Pick it if the question asked about a superficial anterior forearm muscle.

The posterior ulna and interosseous membrane give origin to deep muscles such as extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis. Choose it if the question asked about a deep thumb or index finger extensor.
Correct. Extensor carpi radialis longus arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge.
questions.answerText: Lateral supracondylar ridge of the humerus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does extensor carpi radialis longus insert?
options: Base of metacarpal 2
Base of metacarpal 1
Base of metacarpal 5
Base of metacarpal 3
questions.why: Extensor carpi radialis longus crosses the back of the wrist on the thumb side and inserts on the dorsal base of metacarpal 2, the metacarpal of the index finger. Pulling there extends the wrist and tilts the hand toward the thumb (abduction). Its partner, extensor carpi radialis brevis, lies just beside it and inserts one bone over, on metacarpal 3.
notes: Correct. Extensor carpi radialis longus inserts on the base of metacarpal 2.
The base of metacarpal 1 receives abductor pollicis longus from the deep layer. Pick it if the question asked which muscle moves the thumb away from the palm.
The base of metacarpal 5 receives extensor carpi ulnaris on the little finger side. Choose it if the question asked about the ulnar wrist extensor.
The base of metacarpal 3 receives extensor carpi radialis brevis, the shorter partner. Pick it if the question asked where the brevis inserts.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does extensor carpi ulnaris insert?
options: Base of metacarpal 5
Extensor expansion of digit 5
Base of metacarpal 2
Pisiform and hook of the hamate
questions.why: Extensor carpi ulnaris arises from the lateral epicondyle and the posterior ulna, runs down the ulnar (little finger) side of the back of the forearm, and inserts on the base of metacarpal 5. Because it pulls on the back and the ulnar side of the wrist, it extends the wrist and adducts the hand toward the little finger.
notes: Correct. Extensor carpi ulnaris inserts on the base of metacarpal 5.
The extensor expansion of digit 5 receives extensor digiti minimi, which straightens the little finger. Pick it if the question asked about a finger extensor rather than a wrist extensor.
The base of metacarpal 2 receives extensor carpi radialis longus on the thumb side. Choose it if the question asked about the longer radial wrist extensor.
The pisiform and hook of the hamate receive flexor carpi ulnaris on the front of the wrist. Pick them if the question asked about the ulnar wrist flexor.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does extensor digitorum insert?
options: Middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5
Proximal phalanx of the thumb
Bases of metacarpals 2 to 5
Extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5
questions.why: Extensor digitorum sits in the middle of the superficial posterior forearm and divides into four tendons that cross the back of the hand to digits 2 to 5. Each tendon spreads into an extensor expansion, a flattened hood of tendon over the back of the finger, which carries the pull out to the middle and distal phalanges. That lets one muscle straighten all four fingers and help extend the wrist.
notes: The middle phalanges of digits 2 to 5 receive flexor digitorum superficialis on the palmar side. Pick them if the question asked about the superficial finger flexor.
The proximal phalanx of the thumb receives extensor pollicis brevis. Choose it if the question asked which muscle extends the thumb at its knuckle.
No single muscle inserts on all four metacarpal bases. The wrist extensors attach to single metacarpal bases (2, 3 and 5), so this choice blends the wrist extensors with the finger extensor.
Correct. Extensor digitorum inserts on the extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does the supinator muscle do?
options: Pronates the forearm
Supinates the forearm
Extends the wrist
Flexes the elbow
questions.why: Supinator is a deep posterior forearm muscle that arises from the lateral epicondyle and proximal ulna and wraps around the back of the proximal radius to insert on its lateral surface. When it shortens, it unwinds the radius from across the ulna so the palm turns to face anteriorly, which is supination. It is one of the few posterior compartment muscles that does not extend anything.
notes: Pronation is the opposite movement, done by pronator teres and pronator quadratus in the anterior forearm. Pick it if the question named one of the pronators.
Correct. Supinator turns the palm to face anteriorly.
Wrist extension is done by the extensor carpi muscles, which cross the back of the wrist. Supinator stops on the proximal radius and never reaches the wrist.
Elbow flexion is done by muscles that cross the front of the elbow, such as brachialis, biceps brachii and brachioradialis. Choose it if the question named one of those.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which deep posterior forearm muscle wraps around the proximal radius?
options: Extensor indicis
Abductor pollicis longus
Supinator
Extensor pollicis longus
questions.why: Supinator lies deep in the proximal posterior forearm, under the superficial extensors. Its fibers run from the lateral epicondyle and the proximal ulna and curl around the back and lateral side of the upper radius. That wrapped arrangement is what lets it twist the radius and supinate the forearm.
notes: Extensor indicis arises from the distal posterior ulna and joins the extensor expansion of the index finger. Pick it if the question asked which muscle lets the index finger straighten on its own.

Abductor pollicis longus arises lower on the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane and sends its tendon to the base of metacarpal 1. Pick it if the question asked which deep muscle moves the thumb away from the palm.
Correct. Supinator wraps around the proximal radius.
Extensor pollicis longus arises from the posterior ulna and interosseous membrane and runs to the distal phalanx of the thumb. Choose it if the question asked which muscle straightens the thumb tip.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does abductor pollicis longus insert?
options: Base of metacarpal 2
Proximal phalanx of the thumb
Distal phalanx of the thumb
Base of metacarpal 1
questions.why: Abductor pollicis longus arises from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane, and its tendon curves around the thumb side of the wrist to the base of metacarpal 1. Pulling on the first metacarpal moves the thumb away from the palm (abduction) and also helps extend it. Of the three thumb muscles of the posterior forearm, it inserts on the most proximal bone.
notes: The base of metacarpal 2 receives extensor carpi radialis longus on the back of the wrist. Pick it if the question asked about the longer radial wrist extensor.
The proximal phalanx of the thumb receives extensor pollicis brevis. Pick it if the question asked which muscle extends the thumb at its knuckle.
The distal phalanx of the thumb receives extensor pollicis longus on the back and flexor pollicis longus on the front. Choose it if the question asked which muscles act on the thumb tip.
Correct. Abductor pollicis longus inserts on the base of metacarpal 1.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where does extensor pollicis brevis insert?
options: Distal phalanx of the thumb
Proximal phalanx of the thumb
Base of metacarpal 1
Extensor expansion of digit 2
questions.why: Extensor pollicis brevis arises from the posterior radius and interosseous membrane alongside abductor pollicis longus. Its tendon runs to the base of the proximal phalanx of the thumb, so it extends the thumb at the metacarpophalangeal joint (the thumb's knuckle). Brevis tells you it is the shorter of the two thumb extensors, and it stops one bone short of extensor pollicis longus.
notes: The distal phalanx of the thumb is where extensor pollicis longus inserts. Pick it if the question asked about the long thumb extensor that straightens the tip.
Correct. Extensor pollicis brevis inserts on the proximal phalanx of the thumb.
The base of metacarpal 1 is where abductor pollicis longus inserts. Choose it if the question asked which muscle moves the thumb away from the palm.
The extensor expansion of digit 2 receives extensor indicis, the extra extensor of the index finger. Pick it if the question asked about the pointing finger.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: At which joint does extensor pollicis longus extend the thumb that no other thumb extensor reaches?
options: The metacarpophalangeal joint, the thumb's knuckle
The interphalangeal joint near the tip of the thumb
The wrist joint on the thumb side
The carpometacarpal joint at the base of the thumb
questions.why: Extensor pollicis longus inserts on the base of the distal phalanx of the thumb, so it is the only thumb extensor that can straighten the tip at the interphalangeal joint. Its tendon also crosses the knuckle and the base of the thumb on the way, so it helps extend those joints too. Its tendon forms the ulnar border of the anatomical snuffbox.
notes: The metacarpophalangeal joint is where extensor pollicis brevis does its work, since it stops on the proximal phalanx. Choose it if the question asked about the short thumb extensor.
Correct. Only extensor pollicis longus reaches the distal phalanx to straighten the thumb tip.
The wrist on the thumb side is extended by extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis. Pick it if the question named a muscle with carpi in its name.
The carpometacarpal joint at the base of the thumb is moved by abductor pollicis longus, which inserts on metacarpal 1. Pick it if the question asked where that muscle acts.
questions.answerText: The interphalangeal joint near the tip of the thumb
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What is the action of extensor indicis?
options: Extends the index finger
Adducts the wrist
Extends the little finger
Abducts the thumb
questions.why: Extensor indicis is a small deep posterior muscle that arises from the posterior ulna and interosseous membrane and joins the extensor expansion of digit 2. Indicis refers to the index finger, the pointing finger. Its extra tendon lets the index finger straighten on its own, which is why you can point while the other fingers stay curled.
notes: Correct. Extensor indicis extends the index finger.
Adducting the wrist is done by extensor carpi ulnaris working with flexor carpi ulnaris. Pick it if the name contained carpi ulnaris.
Extending the little finger on its own is the job of extensor digiti minimi. Pick it if the name contained digiti minimi.
Abducting the thumb is done by abductor pollicis longus in the deep posterior layer, along with the short abductor in the hand. Choose it if the name contained pollicis.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: In the muscle name extensor digiti minimi, what does digiti minimi refer to?
options: The middle finger
The thumb
The little finger
The index finger
questions.why: Digiti minimi means the smallest digit, the little finger. Extensor digiti minimi is a slender superficial muscle that lies just medial to extensor digitorum and joins the extensor expansion of digit 5. The same words appear in the hypothenar muscles of the hand, such as abductor digiti minimi, which also act on the little finger.
notes: No forearm muscle is named for the middle finger alone. It is moved by extensor digitorum along with the other fingers, and in the hand it serves as the reference line for spreading the fingers.
The thumb is named by pollicis, as in extensor pollicis longus. Pick this if the name contained pollicis.
Correct. Digiti minimi means the little finger.
The index finger is named by indicis, as in extensor indicis. Choose it if the name contained indicis.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which group lists the deep layer of the posterior forearm?
options: Extensor carpi radialis longus, extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi, extensor carpi ulnaris
Flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus, pronator quadratus
Supinator, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus, extensor indicis
Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: The deep posterior layer lies against the radius, ulna and interosseous membrane. Supinator sits proximally around the radius, and below it four muscles run toward the thumb and index finger: abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis. Most of the deep layer acts on the thumb and index finger, while the superficial layer acts on the wrist and the four fingers together.
notes: These five muscles form the superficial layer of the posterior forearm, most of them arising from the lateral epicondyle. Pick this group if the question asked about the superficial extensors.

Flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus and pronator quadratus form the deep layer of the anterior forearm. Choose them if the question asked about deep muscles on the front of the forearm.
Correct. These five muscles form the deep posterior layer.

Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus and flexor carpi ulnaris are the superficial anterior muscles from the medial epicondyle. Pick them if the question asked about the common flexor origin.
questions.answerText: Supinator, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus, extensor indicis
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which group of muscles arises from the common extensor origin on the lateral epicondyle?
options: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus, extensor indicis
Extensor carpi radialis longus, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis longus, extensor indicis
Extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi, extensor carpi ulnaris
Pronator teres, flexor carpi radialis, palmaris longus, flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: The common extensor origin is a shared tendon on the lateral epicondyle. Extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi and extensor carpi ulnaris all start there and fan down the back of the forearm. Extensor carpi radialis longus is the exception in the superficial group, arising slightly higher on the lateral supracondylar ridge.
notes: These four deep muscles arise from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane, not the humerus. Pick this group if the question asked which posterior muscles act mainly on the thumb and index finger.

This group mixes extensor carpi radialis longus, which arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge, with three deep muscles that arise from the radius, ulna and membrane. None of them use the common extensor tendon.
Correct. These four superficial extensors share the lateral epicondyle origin.
These four superficial anterior muscles arise from the medial epicondyle, the common flexor origin. Choose them if the question asked about the flexor side of the elbow.
questions.answerText: Extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi, extensor carpi ulnaris
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does extensor carpi radialis brevis do at the wrist?
options: Extends and adducts the wrist
Flexes and abducts the wrist
Extends and abducts the wrist
Flexes and adducts the wrist
questions.why: The name gives the action: extensor for straightening, carpi for the wrist, radialis for the thumb side, and brevis because it is shorter than its longus partner. Its tendon crosses the back of the wrist on the thumb side and inserts on the base of metacarpal 3, so it extends the wrist and helps tilt the hand toward the thumb. It works alongside extensor carpi radialis longus.
notes: Extending and adducting the wrist is the action of extensor carpi ulnaris on the little finger side. Pick it if the name contained ulnaris.
Flexing and abducting the wrist is the action of flexor carpi radialis on the front of the forearm. Choose it if the name began with flexor.
Correct. Extensor carpi radialis brevis extends and abducts the wrist.
Flexing and adducting the wrist is the action of flexor carpi ulnaris on the front of the forearm. Pick it if the question named the ulnar wrist flexor.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Extensor carpi radialis longus and extensor carpi radialis brevis share most of their name. What do longus and brevis tell you?
options: Which one lies deeper
Which one is longer
Which one is stronger
Which side of the wrist each crosses
questions.why: Longus means long and brevis means short, so the names compare the lengths of two muscles that otherwise match. Extensor carpi radialis longus starts higher, on the lateral supracondylar ridge, and is the longer of the pair, while brevis starts on the lateral epicondyle. Both extend and abduct the wrist and lie side by side on the thumb side of the back of the forearm.
notes: Depth is named by superficialis and profundus, as in the finger flexors. Both radial wrist extensors are superficial, so their names do not need to separate them by depth.
Correct. Longus and brevis compare length.
Muscle names describe strength only indirectly, through size words such as major and minor. Longus and brevis describe length, and the longer muscle is not automatically the stronger one.
The side a muscle crosses is named by radialis or ulnaris. Both muscles contain radialis, so both cross the wrist on the thumb side.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which superficial posterior forearm muscle sends four tendons across the back of the hand to digits 2 to 5?
options: Extensor carpi ulnaris
Extensor digitorum
Extensor digiti minimi
Extensor indicis
questions.why: Extensor digitorum lies in the middle of the superficial posterior forearm and splits into four tendons above the wrist. These pass under the extensor retinaculum and fan out across the back of the hand to digits 2 to 5, where you can see them stand out when you straighten your fingers. Digitorum means of the digits, which matches its reach to all four fingers.
notes: Extensor carpi ulnaris ends on the base of metacarpal 5 and does not reach the fingers. Pick it if the question asked which muscle extends and adducts the wrist.
Correct. Extensor digitorum sends four tendons to digits 2 to 5.
Extensor digiti minimi sends a single tendon to the little finger. Choose it if the question asked about the extra extensor of digit 5.
Extensor indicis is a deep muscle with a single tendon to the index finger. Pick it if the question asked which muscle lets the index finger straighten on its own.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Unlike the superficial extensors, the deep posterior forearm muscles that move the thumb and index finger mostly arise from where?
options: The common flexor tendon on the medial epicondyle
The olecranon at the point of the elbow
The common extensor tendon on the lateral epicondyle
The posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane
questions.why: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis lie in the deep layer against the bones. They arise from the posterior surfaces of the radius and ulna and from the interosseous membrane between them, rather than from the humerus. Because they start partway down the forearm, they do not cross the elbow and act only at the wrist, thumb and index finger.
notes: The medial epicondyle is the common flexor origin on the anterior side. Choose it if the question asked about the superficial flexors.
The olecranon is where triceps brachii inserts, and it gives a minor origin to flexor carpi ulnaris. Pick it if the question asked for the insertion of triceps.
The lateral epicondyle is the common extensor origin for the superficial layer. Pick it if the question asked where extensor digitorum or extensor carpi ulnaris begins.
Correct. The deep thumb and index muscles arise from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane.
questions.answerText: The posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares extensor carpi radialis longus and extensor carpi radialis brevis?
options: Longus arises from the lateral epicondyle and inserts on metacarpal 3; brevis arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge and inserts on metacarpal 2
Longus lies in the deep layer; brevis lies in the superficial layer
Longus arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge and inserts on metacarpal 2; brevis arises from the lateral epicondyle and inserts on metacarpal 3
Longus extends and abducts the wrist; brevis flexes and adducts the wrist
questions.why: The two radial wrist extensors lie side by side and do the same job, extending the wrist and tilting it toward the thumb. Longus starts higher, on the lateral supracondylar ridge, and ends on metacarpal 2, while brevis starts on the lateral epicondyle with the other common extensors and ends one bone over on metacarpal 3. The longer muscle starts higher and ends closer to the thumb.
notes: This swaps the attachments of the two muscles. It would be right only if the names were reversed, so tie longus to the higher origin on the supracondylar ridge.
Both muscles are in the superficial layer of the posterior forearm. The deep layer holds supinator and the thumb and index finger muscles.
Correct. Longus runs from the supracondylar ridge to metacarpal 2, and brevis from the lateral epicondyle to metacarpal 3.
Both muscles extend and abduct the wrist. Flexing and adducting is the action of flexor carpi ulnaris on the front of the forearm.
questions.answerText: Longus arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge and inserts on metacarpal 2; brevis arises from the lateral epicondyle and inserts on metacarpal 3
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which pair of muscles works together to adduct the wrist, tilting the hand toward the little finger side?
options: Flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis longus
Flexor carpi ulnaris and flexor carpi radialis
Extensor carpi radialis brevis and extensor carpi ulnaris
Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: Adduction of the wrist (ulnar deviation) needs muscles on the little finger side. Flexor carpi ulnaris crosses the front of the wrist on that side and extensor carpi ulnaris crosses the back. When both contract together, flexion and extension cancel out and the hand tilts straight toward the little finger, which is why both share ulnaris in their names.
notes: Flexor carpi radialis and extensor carpi radialis longus both cross the wrist on the thumb side, so together they abduct the wrist. Pick this pair if the question asked about tilting the hand toward the thumb.
Flexor carpi ulnaris and flexor carpi radialis both cross the front of the wrist, one on each side, so together they flex the wrist straight forward. Pick them for pure wrist flexion.
Extensor carpi radialis brevis and extensor carpi ulnaris both cross the back of the wrist, one on each side, so together they extend the wrist straight back. Choose them for pure wrist extension.
Correct. The two ulnaris muscles combine to adduct the wrist.
questions.answerText: Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris
