review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares extensor pollicis brevis and extensor pollicis longus?
options: Brevis inserts on the proximal phalanx of the thumb; longus inserts on the distal phalanx
Brevis inserts on the distal phalanx of the thumb; longus inserts on the proximal phalanx
Both insert on the distal phalanx and differ only in where they arise
Brevis inserts on metacarpal 1; longus inserts on the proximal phalanx of the thumb
questions.why: Both muscles extend the thumb from the deep posterior forearm, but they stop at different bones. Extensor pollicis brevis, the short one, ends on the proximal phalanx and extends the thumb at its knuckle (the metacarpophalangeal joint). Extensor pollicis longus, the long one, continues to the distal phalanx and is the only extensor that straightens the thumb tip at the interphalangeal joint.
notes: Correct. Brevis ends on the proximal phalanx and longus on the distal phalanx.
This reverses the two insertions. The short muscle (brevis) stops on the nearer bone and the long muscle (longus) reaches the tip.
They differ in insertion as well as origin. If both reached the distal phalanx, losing one would not change which thumb joint could still be straightened.
Metacarpal 1 is the insertion of abductor pollicis longus, not extensor pollicis brevis. Pick a statement about metacarpal 1 only if it named the abductor.
questions.answerText: Brevis inserts on the proximal phalanx of the thumb; longus inserts on the distal phalanx
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Most people can straighten the index finger or the little finger on its own while the other fingers stay curled. What anatomical feature allows this?
options: Those two fingers receive tendons from the extensor retinaculum
Those two fingers have no flexor digitorum profundus tendons
Those two fingers lack an extensor expansion
Each has an extra extensor besides extensor digitorum
questions.why: Extensor digitorum sends tendons to all four fingers, so on its own it tends to straighten them together. The index finger also receives extensor indicis and the little finger also receives extensor digiti minimi, and each of these joins the extensor expansion of its finger. That extra, separate tendon is what lets you point with the index finger or lift the little finger by itself.
notes: The extensor retinaculum is a band across the back of the wrist that holds the extensor tendons down. It does not give rise to tendons, so pick it if the question asked what keeps the extensor tendons from bowstringing.
All four fingers have flexor digitorum profundus tendons, which bend the fingertips. Removing a flexor would not add any extension, so this choice confuses the flexor and extensor sides.
Every finger has an extensor expansion, the hood over the back of the finger that carries the extensor pull to the phalanges. Without one, a finger could not be straightened at all.
Correct. Extensor indicis and extensor digiti minimi give these two fingers independent extension.
questions.answerText: Each has an extra extensor besides extensor digitorum
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the two main supinators of the forearm, supinator and biceps brachii?
options: Supinator supinates the forearm from the posterior side; biceps brachii pronates it from the anterior arm
Both muscles arise from the lateral epicondyle of the humerus and insert on the styloid process of the radius
Supinator pulls on the radial tuberosity from the anterior arm; biceps brachii wraps the proximal radius from the posterior forearm
Supinator wraps the proximal radius from the posterior forearm; biceps brachii pulls on the radial tuberosity from the anterior arm
questions.why: Both muscles turn the palm to face anteriorly, but they come from different regions. Supinator is a deep posterior forearm muscle that curls around the proximal radius from the lateral epicondyle and ulna. Biceps brachii is an anterior arm muscle whose tendon inserts on the radial tuberosity, and it is the stronger supinator, especially when the elbow is bent.
notes: Biceps brachii supinates as well as flexing the elbow. Pronation belongs to pronator teres and pronator quadratus, so pick a statement about pronation only if it named one of those.

Only supinator uses the lateral epicondyle, and neither muscle reaches the styloid process of the radius, which is where brachioradialis inserts. Choose the styloid process for a question about brachioradialis.
This swaps the two muscles' locations and attachments. Biceps brachii is the anterior arm muscle on the radial tuberosity, and supinator is the posterior forearm muscle that wraps the radius.
Correct. Supinator wraps the proximal radius from the posterior forearm, and biceps brachii pulls on the radial tuberosity from the anterior arm.
questions.answerText: Supinator wraps the proximal radius from the posterior forearm; biceps brachii pulls on the radial tuberosity from the anterior arm
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which deep posterior forearm muscle does not move the thumb or any finger?
options: Abductor pollicis longus
Extensor indicis
Supinator
Extensor pollicis longus
questions.why: Supinator attaches entirely within the proximal forearm, running from the lateral epicondyle and proximal ulna to the proximal radius. Because it never crosses the wrist, it cannot move the hand or digits, and its only job is rotating the radius to supinate the forearm. The other four deep posterior muscles all send tendons into the thumb or the index finger.
notes: Abductor pollicis longus sends its tendon to the base of metacarpal 1 and moves the thumb away from the palm. Pick it if the question asked which deep muscle abducts the thumb.
Extensor indicis joins the extensor expansion of the index finger and straightens it. Choose it if the question asked which muscle lets you point.
Correct. Supinator acts only on the forearm.
Extensor pollicis longus reaches the distal phalanx of the thumb and straightens the thumb tip. Pick it if the question asked which muscle extends the thumb's interphalangeal joint.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Extensor digitorum arises from the lateral epicondyle and inserts on the extensor expansions of digits 2 to 5. Which joints can it extend?
options: The thumb joints and the wrist
The finger joints only
The finger joints and the wrist
The wrist only
questions.why: A muscle can act on every joint its tendons cross. Extensor digitorum crosses the back of the wrist and then the knuckles and finger joints of digits 2 to 5, so it straightens the fingers and also helps extend the wrist. This is why the course notes list its action as extending both the fingers and the wrist.
notes: The thumb is extended by extensor pollicis longus and brevis. Extensor digitorum sends no tendon to the thumb, so pick this choice only for a muscle with pollicis in its name.
Its tendons have to cross the back of the wrist to reach the fingers, so the muscle also pulls the wrist into extension. This choice overlooks the joints a tendon passes on its way.
Correct. Its tendons cross the back of the wrist and the finger joints, so it extends both.
A muscle that extended only the wrist would insert on a metacarpal, like the extensor carpi muscles. Extensor digitorum continues into the fingers, so it moves them too.
questions.answerText: The finger joints and the wrist
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does each part of the name abductor pollicis longus tell you?
options: It moves the thumb away from the palm, acts on the thumb, and is the long member of a pair
It moves the wrist away from the body, acts on the wrist, and is the long member of a pair
It moves the index finger away from the palm, acts on the index finger, and lies deep
It moves the thumb toward the palm, acts on the thumb, and is the long member of a pair
questions.why: Abductor means it moves a part away, pollicis means the thumb, and longus means long. Abductor pollicis longus starts in the posterior forearm and ends on metacarpal 1, pulling the thumb away from the palm. Its partner, abductor pollicis brevis, is a short thenar muscle in the hand that makes a similar movement, and longus and brevis tell the two apart.
notes: Correct. Abductor, pollicis and longus give the action, the digit and the relative length.
Wrist muscles carry carpi in their names, as in extensor carpi radialis longus. Pollicis tells you this muscle acts on the thumb, not the wrist.
The index finger is named by indicis, as in extensor indicis. Pollicis always refers to the thumb.
Moving toward is adduction, not abduction. That would describe adductor pollicis in the web space of the hand.
questions.answerText: It moves the thumb away from the palm, acts on the thumb, and is the long member of a pair
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A muscle arises from the lateral supracondylar ridge, crosses the back of the wrist on the thumb side and inserts on the base of metacarpal 2. Which action would you predict at the wrist?
options: Flexion and abduction
Flexion and adduction
Extension and adduction
Extension and abduction
questions.why: Crossing the back of the wrist means the muscle extends it, and crossing on the thumb side means it tilts the hand toward the thumb, which is abduction. These attachments belong to extensor carpi radialis longus. Reading the side and the surface a tendon crosses lets you predict the action before you recall the name.
notes: Flexion would need a tendon crossing the front of the wrist, like flexor carpi radialis. This muscle is on the back.
Flexion and adduction describe flexor carpi ulnaris, which crosses the front of the wrist on the little finger side. Both the surface and the side are wrong for this muscle.
Adduction would need a tendon on the little finger side, like extensor carpi ulnaris. This tendon crosses on the thumb side.
Correct. A tendon on the back and thumb side of the wrist extends and abducts it.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the superficial and deep layers of the posterior forearm?
options: The superficial layer mostly arises from the radius, ulna and interosseous membrane and moves the thumb; the deep layer mostly arises from the lateral epicondyle and moves the wrist
The superficial layer mostly arises from the lateral epicondyle and moves the wrist and fingers; the deep layer arises lower and mostly moves the thumb and index finger
Both layers arise from the lateral epicondyle, and they differ only in which of the four fingers they extend
The superficial layer mostly arises from the medial epicondyle and flexes the wrist; the deep layer mostly arises from the lateral epicondyle and extends it
questions.why: The superficial extensors (extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor digitorum, extensor digiti minimi and extensor carpi ulnaris) share the lateral epicondyle origin and act on the wrist and digits 2 to 5. The deep layer lies against the bones, arising from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane, and mostly moves the thumb and index finger. Supinator is the one deep muscle that acts on the forearm instead.
notes: This swaps the two layers. The muscles from the lateral epicondyle are the superficial ones, and the bone and membrane origins belong to the deep layer.
Correct. The two layers differ in where they arise and in which parts of the hand they move.
The deep layer does not arise from the lateral epicondyle, apart from part of supinator. Its thumb and index muscles start lower, on the radius, ulna and membrane.
The medial epicondyle and wrist flexion belong to the anterior forearm. Both layers of the posterior forearm are on the extensor side.
questions.answerText: The superficial layer mostly arises from the lateral epicondyle and moves the wrist and fingers; the deep layer arises lower and mostly moves the thumb and index finger
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which list orders the three posterior thumb muscles by where they insert, from the most proximal bone to the most distal?
options: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis
Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus
Extensor pollicis brevis, abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis longus
Extensor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, abductor pollicis longus
questions.why: Abductor pollicis longus stops on the base of metacarpal 1, extensor pollicis brevis continues to the proximal phalanx, and extensor pollicis longus reaches the distal phalanx. Each muscle therefore acts one joint farther out than the last: the base of the thumb, then the knuckle, then the tip. Knowing this order lets you work out which thumb movement is lost when one tendon is cut.
notes: This swaps the two extensors. Brevis, the short one, ends on the proximal phalanx, and longus continues to the distal phalanx.
Correct. The insertions run from metacarpal 1 to the proximal phalanx to the distal phalanx.
This places extensor pollicis brevis before abductor pollicis longus. The abductor stops on metacarpal 1, which is proximal to the proximal phalanx where brevis inserts.
This is the correct order written backward, from distal to proximal. Pick it if the question asked for the order starting at the tip of the thumb.
questions.answerText: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does each part of the name extensor carpi ulnaris tell you?
options: It straightens a joint, acts on the fingers, and lies on the ulnar side
It straightens a joint, acts on the wrist, and lies on the ulnar side
It bends a joint, acts on the wrist, and lies on the ulnar side
It straightens a joint, acts on the wrist, and lies on the radial side
questions.why: Extensor names the action (straightening a joint), carpi names the wrist, and ulnaris places the muscle on the ulnar (little finger) side. Together they predict exactly what the muscle does: it extends the wrist and, because it pulls on the ulnar side, adducts the hand toward the little finger. It inserts on the base of metacarpal 5.
notes: Muscles that act on the fingers carry digitorum or a specific finger name, as in extensor digitorum. Carpi means the wrist.
Correct. Extensor, carpi and ulnaris give the action, the joint and the side.
Bending a joint is flexion, named by flexor, as in flexor carpi ulnaris on the front of the forearm. Pick this if the name began with flexor.
The radial side is named by radialis, as in extensor carpi radialis longus. Ulnaris places this muscle on the opposite side.
questions.answerText: It straightens a joint, acts on the wrist, and lies on the ulnar side
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which of these posterior forearm muscles crosses both the elbow and the wrist?
options: Abductor pollicis longus
Supinator
Extensor carpi radialis brevis
Extensor pollicis longus
questions.why: Extensor carpi radialis brevis arises above the elbow on the lateral epicondyle and inserts below the wrist on metacarpal 3, so its path crosses both joints. Supinator never reaches the wrist, and the deep thumb muscles start on the radius, ulna and interosseous membrane below the elbow. Knowing which joints a muscle crosses tells you which joints it can move.
notes: Abductor pollicis longus arises from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane below the elbow. It crosses the wrist on its way to metacarpal 1 but does not cross the elbow.
Supinator starts at the elbow region but stops on the proximal radius, so it never crosses the wrist. Pick it if the question asked which posterior muscle acts only on the forearm.
Correct. It runs from the lateral epicondyle to metacarpal 3, crossing both the elbow and the wrist.
Extensor pollicis longus arises from the posterior ulna and interosseous membrane below the elbow. It crosses the wrist but not the elbow.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which description of extensor digiti minimi is accurate?
options: A slender superficial muscle that extends the little finger
A hypothenar muscle in the hand that abducts the little finger
A deep muscle from the posterior ulna that extends the index finger
A superficial muscle that inserts on metacarpal 5 and adducts the wrist
questions.why: Extensor digiti minimi is a thin superficial muscle that arises from the common extensor origin and lies just medial to extensor digitorum. Its tendon joins the extensor expansion of digit 5, giving the little finger an extensor of its own. That is why you can lift the little finger by itself.
notes: Correct. Extensor digiti minimi is a slender superficial extensor of the little finger.
This describes abductor digiti minimi, an intrinsic hypothenar muscle of the hand. Choose it if the name began with abductor.
This describes extensor indicis, the deep extensor of the index finger. Pick it if the name contained indicis.
This describes extensor carpi ulnaris, which ends on metacarpal 5 and moves the wrist rather than the finger. Pick it if the name contained carpi ulnaris.
questions.answerText: A slender superficial muscle that extends the little finger
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A tennis player has pain on the lateral side of the elbow that flares when he extends his wrist against resistance or grips his racket. Which structure is most likely irritated?
options: The biceps brachii tendon at the radial tuberosity
The common extensor tendon at the lateral epicondyle
The triceps brachii tendon at the olecranon
The common flexor tendon at the medial epicondyle
questions.why: Tennis elbow (lateral epicondylitis) is irritation of the shared tendon where the superficial extensors attach to the lateral epicondyle. Resisted wrist extension loads that tendon directly. Gripping also hurts because the wrist extensors contract to hold the wrist steady while the finger flexors squeeze, so every grip pulls on the sore spot.
notes: The biceps tendon inserts on the radial tuberosity at the front of the elbow. Irritation there would hurt with resisted elbow flexion and supination, not wrist extension.
Correct. Lateral elbow pain with resisted wrist extension and gripping points to the common extensor origin.
The triceps tendon inserts on the olecranon at the back of the elbow. Irritation there would hurt with resisted elbow extension rather than wrist extension.
The common flexor tendon at the medial epicondyle is the site of golfer's elbow, which hurts on the inner elbow with resisted wrist flexion. Pick it if the pain were medial.
questions.answerText: The common extensor tendon at the lateral epicondyle
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: After a cut on the back of the thumb, a patient can straighten the thumb at its knuckle but cannot straighten the tip. Which tendon was most likely cut?
options: Extensor pollicis longus
Abductor pollicis longus
Flexor pollicis longus
Extensor pollicis brevis
questions.why: Straightening the thumb tip happens at the interphalangeal joint, and the only extensor that reaches the distal phalanx is extensor pollicis longus. The knuckle still straightens because extensor pollicis brevis, which inserts on the proximal phalanx, is intact. Losing only the tip movement points to the long extensor tendon.
notes: Correct. Extensor pollicis longus is the only extensor of the thumb tip.
Abductor pollicis longus inserts on metacarpal 1 and moves the thumb away from the palm. A cut there would weaken thumb abduction rather than tip extension.
Flexor pollicis longus bends the thumb tip from the palm side. A cut there would leave the patient unable to bend the tip, and the cut would be on the front of the thumb.

If extensor pollicis brevis were cut, extension at the knuckle would weaken, but the long extensor could still straighten the tip. Pick it if the scenario described weak knuckle extension with the tip working.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: When you squeeze a fist hard, you can feel the muscles on the back of your forearm tighten even though your fingers are bending. What are those posterior muscles doing?
options: Holding the wrist extended so the flexors pull efficiently
Pronating the forearm so the fist rotates palm down
Relaxing completely so the finger flexors are not opposed
Flexing the fingers together with the anterior forearm muscles
questions.why: The long finger flexors cross the wrist before they reach the fingers, so when they contract they would also bend the wrist. The wrist extensors (extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis and extensor carpi ulnaris) contract at the same time to hold the wrist slightly extended, acting as synergists that stabilize the joint. With the wrist held steady, the flexors' pull goes into the fingers and the grip is stronger.
notes: Correct. The wrist extensors stabilize the wrist so the grip is strong.
Pronation is done by pronator teres and pronator quadratus on the front of the forearm. Making a fist does not require rotating the forearm.
The tightening you feel shows these muscles are contracting, not relaxing. If they relaxed, the finger flexors would pull the wrist into flexion and the grip would weaken.
The posterior muscles are extensors, so they cannot flex the fingers. Finger flexion comes from flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus on the front of the forearm.
questions.answerText: Holding the wrist extended so the flexors pull efficiently
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A hitchhiker holds the thumb up and back, and tendons stand out around a small hollow at the base of the thumb on the back of the wrist. Which muscles do these tendons belong to?
options: Extensor carpi radialis longus, extensor carpi radialis brevis, extensor carpi ulnaris
Flexor pollicis longus, flexor pollicis brevis, abductor pollicis brevis
Extensor digitorum, extensor indicis, extensor digiti minimi
Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus
questions.why: Pulling the thumb up and back uses the three deep posterior muscles that reach the thumb. Their tendons frame the anatomical snuffbox, the small hollow at the base of the thumb: abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis on one side, and extensor pollicis longus on the other. These muscles arise from the posterior radius, ulna and interosseous membrane and act only on the thumb.
notes: These muscles extend the wrist and insert on metacarpals 2, 3 and 5. Pick them if the question asked about bending the wrist back rather than moving the thumb.
These muscles bend the thumb or move it from the palm side, and their tendons are on the front of the hand. Pick them if the question asked about gripping with the thumb.
These muscles extend digits 2 to 5, and their tendons run across the back of the hand to the fingers rather than the thumb. Choose them if the question asked about straightening the fingers.
Correct. These three thumb tendons outline the anatomical snuffbox.
questions.answerText: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A right-handed carpenter tightens a screw by turning the screwdriver clockwise, rotating the palm from facing down to facing up with the elbow bent. Which two muscles drive this movement?
options: Pronator teres and pronator quadratus
Brachialis and brachioradialis
Supinator and biceps brachii
Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis
questions.why: Turning the palm from facing down to facing up is supination, which unrolls the radius from across the ulna. Supinator wraps the proximal radius and does this at any elbow angle, while biceps brachii adds a powerful pull on the radial tuberosity, especially with the elbow bent. That is why screws are easier to drive with the right hand and a flexed elbow.
notes: Pronator teres and pronator quadratus turn the palm from up to down, which would loosen the screw with the right hand. Pick them for the opposite rotation.
Brachialis and brachioradialis bend the elbow but do not rotate the forearm. Choose them if the carpenter were lifting a tool toward the body.
Correct. Supinator and biceps brachii supinate the forearm.
The radial wrist extensors bend the wrist back and tilt it toward the thumb. They do not turn the palm over, so pick them only for a question about wrist movement.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A patient can straighten all four fingers together but cannot lift the index finger alone while the other fingers stay curled into the palm. Which muscle is most likely not working?
options: Extensor digiti minimi
Extensor indicis
Extensor pollicis longus
Extensor digitorum
questions.why: Extensor digitorum straightens all four fingers together, and the patient can still do that, so it is working. Lifting the index finger alone while the others stay curled depends on extensor indicis, the deep muscle that adds a separate tendon to the extensor expansion of the index finger. Losing that independent movement while group extension is normal points to extensor indicis.
notes: Extensor digiti minimi gives the little finger independent extension. Choose it if the patient could not lift the little finger by itself.
Correct. Extensor indicis gives the index finger independent extension.
Extensor pollicis longus straightens the thumb tip and does not act on the index finger. Pick it if the patient could not straighten the tip of the thumb.
Extensor digitorum is the muscle that straightens all four fingers together, which this patient can still do. Pick it if the patient could not straighten any of the fingers.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A deep cut on the thumb side of the back of the wrist severs the tendon that inserts on the base of metacarpal 1. Which movement is most weakened?
options: Moving the thumb away from the palm
Bending the tip of the thumb
Tilting the wrist toward the little finger
Straightening the index finger
questions.why: The tendon that inserts on the base of metacarpal 1 belongs to abductor pollicis longus. Pulling on the first metacarpal swings the thumb away from the palm, so cutting this tendon weakens thumb abduction. Some abduction remains because abductor pollicis brevis, a short thenar muscle in the hand, makes a similar movement.
notes: Correct. Abductor pollicis longus moves the thumb away from the palm.
Bending the thumb tip is the job of flexor pollicis longus on the palm side. A cut on the back of the wrist would not affect it.
Tilting the wrist toward the little finger is done by extensor carpi ulnaris and flexor carpi ulnaris on the opposite side of the wrist from this cut.
Straightening the index finger depends on extensor digitorum and extensor indicis, which insert on the extensor expansion of digit 2, not on metacarpal 1.
questions.answerText: Moving the thumb away from the palm
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: When a patient extends the wrist, the hand drifts toward the thumb side instead of lifting straight back. Weakness of which muscle best explains this?
options: Extensor digitorum
Extensor carpi radialis longus
Extensor carpi ulnaris
Flexor carpi ulnaris
questions.why: Straight wrist extension depends on balanced pull from the radial extensors on the thumb side and extensor carpi ulnaris on the little finger side. If extensor carpi ulnaris is weak, the radial extensors pull unopposed, so the hand extends and tilts toward the thumb at the same time. Picturing each tendon as a pull on one corner of the wrist lets you predict the drift.
notes: Extensor digitorum pulls through the middle of the back of the hand toward all four fingers, so its weakness would weaken extension without tilting the hand to one side.

Weak extensor carpi radialis longus would reduce the pull on the thumb side, so extensor carpi ulnaris would tend to tilt the extending hand toward the little finger. Pick it if the scenario described that ulnar drift.
Correct. Without extensor carpi ulnaris, the radial extensors tilt the extending hand toward the thumb.
Flexor carpi ulnaris is on the front of the forearm and flexes the wrist, so it does not take part in wrist extension. Choose it if the hand drifted toward the thumb during wrist flexion.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: After a fall on an outstretched hand, a clinician presses into the anatomical snuffbox to check for a scaphoid fracture. Where is the anatomical snuffbox?
options: The groove between the tubercles of the proximal humerus
The tunnel on the palm side of the wrist under a fibrous band
The hollow on the back of the wrist at the base of the thumb
The pit on the back of the humerus above the elbow
questions.why: The anatomical snuffbox is a small hollow on the back of the wrist at the base of the thumb, which shows clearly when the thumb is extended. The scaphoid lies in its floor. Tenderness there after a fall is the classic clue to a scaphoid fracture.
notes: The groove between the tubercles is the intertubercular sulcus near the shoulder. It would be right for a question about the groove holding a biceps tendon.
The tunnel on the palm side of the wrist under the flexor retinaculum is the carpal tunnel. Pick it for a question about where the median nerve and flexor tendons enter the hand.
Correct. The snuffbox is the hollow at the base of the thumb on the back of the wrist.
The pit on the back of the humerus above the elbow is the olecranon fossa. Choose it for a question about where the olecranon rests when the elbow straightens.
questions.answerText: The hollow on the back of the wrist at the base of the thumb
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which nerve passes through the carpal tunnel along with the long flexor tendons of the fingers and thumb?
options: The radial nerve
The median nerve
The axillary nerve
The ulnar nerve
questions.why: The carpal tunnel is the passage between the carpal bones and the flexor retinaculum, a strong fibrous band that roofs it on the palm side of the wrist. The long flexor tendons and the median nerve travel through it into the hand. When the tunnel narrows, the median nerve is squeezed, which is carpal tunnel syndrome.
notes: The radial nerve runs in the radial groove on the back of the humerus. Pick it for a question about a fracture of the humeral shaft.
Correct. The median nerve runs through the carpal tunnel.
The axillary nerve wraps around the surgical neck of the humerus near the shoulder. It would be right for a question about a fracture of the surgical neck.
The ulnar nerve passes behind the medial epicondyle at the elbow and enters the hand outside the carpal tunnel. Choose it for a question about the funny bone.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which group of intrinsic hand muscles spreads the fingers apart (abducts them) away from the middle finger?
options: The lumbricals
The adductor pollicis
The palmar interossei
The dorsal interossei
questions.why: The dorsal interossei lie between the metacarpals on the back of the hand and pull the fingers away from the middle finger, which is the reference line for abduction in the hand. The memory aid DAB stands for Dorsal interossei ABduct, and its partner PAD stands for Palmar interossei ADduct. Together the two groups spread and close the fingers.
notes: The lumbricals flex the knuckles (metacarpophalangeal joints) while extending the fingers. They would be the answer if the question asked which muscles produce the tabletop position of the hand.
The adductor pollicis is a single muscle in the web space that pulls the thumb toward the palm. Choose it if the question asked which muscle adducts the thumb.
The palmar interossei pull the fingers back toward the middle finger, which is adduction. Pick them if the question asked which muscles bring the fingers together.
Correct. The dorsal interossei abduct the fingers.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which three muscles make up the thenar eminence, the bulge at the base of the thumb?
options: Abductor pollicis longus, extensor pollicis brevis, extensor pollicis longus
Abductor digiti minimi, flexor digiti minimi brevis, opponens digiti minimi
Lumbricals, palmar interossei, dorsal interossei
Abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis
questions.why: The thenar eminence is the fleshy pad at the base of the thumb, formed by three short intrinsic muscles that lie entirely within the hand. Abductor pollicis brevis moves the thumb away from the palm, flexor pollicis brevis bends it at the knuckle, and opponens pollicis rotates it across the palm to meet the fingers. All three carry pollicis in their names because they act on the thumb.
notes: These three muscles act on the thumb but arise in the posterior forearm, so they are not part of the thenar pad. Choose them if the question asked which tendons outline the anatomical snuffbox.
These three muscles form the hypothenar eminence on the little finger side of the palm. Pick them if the question asked about the bulge at the base of the little finger.

The lumbricals and interossei are the midpalmar muscles that lie between the metacarpals and along the flexor tendons. Pick them if the question asked which intrinsic muscles move digits 2 to 5 at the knuckles or spread the fingers.
Correct. These three short thumb muscles form the thenar eminence.
questions.answerText: Abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which muscle belongs to the hypothenar group?
options: Adductor pollicis
Opponens pollicis
Abductor pollicis brevis
Opponens digiti minimi
questions.why: The hypothenar group forms the fleshy bulge on the little finger (ulnar) side of the palm. Its three muscles are abductor digiti minimi, flexor digiti minimi brevis and opponens digiti minimi, and all of them carry digiti minimi in their names because they move the little finger. Opponens digiti minimi draws the little finger toward the thumb to help cup the palm.
notes: Adductor pollicis lies deep in the web space between the thumb and index finger and pulls the thumb toward the palm. Choose it if the question asked which muscle squeezes the thumb against the side of the hand.
Opponens pollicis is a thenar muscle that rotates the thumb across the palm. Pick it if the question asked about the thumb rather than the little finger.
Abductor pollicis brevis is a thenar muscle that moves the thumb away from the palm. Pick it if the question asked about the thenar eminence.
Correct. Opponens digiti minimi is one of the three hypothenar muscles.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: How many lumbrical muscles are in each hand?
options: Two
Five
Three
Four
questions.why: There are four lumbricals, one for each finger from the index to the little finger. Each is a small, worm-shaped muscle (lumbricus means earthworm) that arises from a tendon of flexor digitorum profundus in the palm and inserts on the extensor expansion of its finger. The thumb has no lumbrical.
notes: Two is too few, since each finger from digit 2 to digit 5 has its own lumbrical. This number comes from counting only part of the hand.
Five would include the thumb, but the thumb has no lumbrical because flexor digitorum profundus, the tendon the lumbricals arise from, does not go to the thumb.
Three is a common slip if you skip the index or little finger. Every finger from digit 2 to digit 5 has a lumbrical, which makes four.
Correct. There are four lumbricals, one for each of digits 2 to 5.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What do the lumbricals do to digits 2 to 5?
options: Extend the metacarpophalangeal joints and flex the interphalangeal joints
Flex both the metacarpophalangeal and interphalangeal joints
Spread the fingers apart from the middle finger
Flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints
questions.why: The lumbricals bend the knuckles (metacarpophalangeal joints) while straightening the finger joints (interphalangeal joints). The course notes put it simply: they flex the knuckles and extend the fingers. This produces the tabletop position you use to hold a pen or a playing card.
notes: This is the reverse of the lumbrical action. It describes a claw-like position, which the fingers fall into when the small intrinsic hand muscles are not working.
Flexing every finger joint at once is the job of the long flexors, flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus, as in making a fist. Pick this if the question named those forearm muscles.
Spreading the fingers away from the middle finger is abduction, done by the dorsal interossei. Choose it if the question asked about the dorsal interossei.
Correct. The lumbricals flex the knuckles and straighten the finger joints.
questions.answerText: Flex the metacarpophalangeal joints and extend the interphalangeal joints
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which intrinsic hand muscles lie between the metacarpals and spread the fingers apart?
options: Palmar interossei
Dorsal interossei
Lumbricals
Hypothenar muscles
questions.why: The dorsal interossei fill the spaces between the metacarpals and are felt from the back of the hand. They abduct the fingers, spreading them away from a line through the middle finger. The course notes give the memory aid DAB: dorsal interossei abduct.
notes: The palmar interossei also lie between the metacarpals but on the palm side, and they adduct the fingers toward the middle finger. Pick them for squeezing the fingers together (PAD).
Correct. The dorsal interossei abduct the fingers.
The lumbricals lie in the palm alongside the flexor digitorum profundus tendons and flex the knuckles while extending the finger joints. Choose them for the tabletop position.
The hypothenar muscles form the bulge on the little finger side of the palm and move only the little finger. Pick them if the question asked about that bulge.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Abduction and adduction of the fingers are measured from which reference line?
options: The midline of the body
A line through the thumb
A line through the middle finger
A line through the little finger
questions.why: In the hand, abduction means spreading a finger away from a line through the middle finger, and adduction means bringing it back toward that line. The course notes stress that this reference is the middle finger, not the midline of the body. That is why spreading the fingers is called abduction even for the index finger, which moves toward the thumb.
notes: The body midline is the reference for most limb movements, such as raising the arm out to the side. Students choose it by habit, but the fingers use their own reference line.
The thumb moves in its own planes and is not the reference for the other fingers. Using it would make every finger movement toward the thumb look like adduction, which is not how the terms are used.
Correct. Finger abduction and adduction are measured from the middle finger.
The little finger sits at the edge of the hand, so it cannot serve as a central reference line. This choice usually comes from mixing up the reference line with the hypothenar side of the hand.
questions.answerText: A line through the middle finger
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Where is adductor pollicis located?
options: In the bulge on the little finger side of the palm
Between the metacarpals on the back of the hand
In the deep layer of the anterior forearm
In the web space between the thumb and index finger
questions.why: Adductor pollicis is a fan-shaped muscle that lies deep in the palm, in the web space between the thumb and the index finger. It pulls the thumb toward the palm, which is the movement you use to pinch a key between the thumb and the side of the index finger. The course notes list it as a single muscle of its own, separate from the thenar group.
notes: The bulge on the little finger side is the hypothenar eminence, made of abductor digiti minimi, flexor digiti minimi brevis and opponens digiti minimi. Pick it if the question asked about the little finger muscles.
The spaces between the metacarpals on the back of the hand hold the dorsal interossei. Choose this if the question asked which muscles spread the fingers.
The deep anterior forearm holds flexor digitorum profundus, flexor pollicis longus and pronator quadratus. Adductor pollicis is an intrinsic muscle that lies entirely within the hand.
Correct. Adductor pollicis lies in the thumb web space.
questions.answerText: In the web space between the thumb and index finger
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which structure forms the roof of the carpal tunnel?
options: Extensor retinaculum
Flexor retinaculum
Bicipital aponeurosis
Palmar aponeurosis
questions.why: The carpal bones form a curved trough on the front of the wrist, and the flexor retinaculum is the strong fibrous band that bridges across the top of it. Together they create the carpal tunnel, a closed passage for the long flexor tendons and the median nerve. Because the retinaculum does not stretch, swelling inside the tunnel has nowhere to go.
notes: The extensor retinaculum is a band across the back of the wrist that holds down the extensor tendons. Choose it if the question asked about the dorsal side of the wrist.
Correct. The flexor retinaculum is the roof of the carpal tunnel.
The bicipital aponeurosis is a sheet from the biceps brachii tendon that crosses the front of the elbow over the cubital fossa. Pick it if the question asked about the elbow rather than the wrist.

The palmar aponeurosis is a triangular sheet of deep fascia in the palm, lying beyond the tunnel and continuous with the palmaris longus tendon. Pick it if the question asked which fascia covers the palm.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What passes through the carpal tunnel?
options: The median nerve and the long flexor tendons of the fingers and thumb
The radial nerve and the extensor tendons of the fingers
The radial artery and the palmaris longus tendon
The ulnar nerve and the ulnar artery
questions.why: The carpal tunnel is a narrow passage on the front of the wrist, with the carpal bones forming its floor and sides and the flexor retinaculum forming its roof. Through it run the median nerve and nine tendons: four from flexor digitorum superficialis, four from flexor digitorum profundus and one from flexor pollicis longus. With so much packed into a space with rigid walls, swelling inside it presses on the median nerve.
notes: Correct. The median nerve and nine long flexor tendons pass through the tunnel.
The extensor tendons run across the back of the wrist under the extensor retinaculum. Choose this if the question asked what the extensor retinaculum holds down.
The radial artery runs on the thumb side of the wrist, and the palmaris longus tendon passes in front of the flexor retinaculum. Neither goes through the tunnel.

The ulnar nerve and ulnar artery cross the front of the wrist on the little finger side, superficial to the flexor retinaculum, so they stay outside the tunnel. Pick them if the question asked what passes near the pisiform outside the tunnel.
questions.answerText: The median nerve and the long flexor tendons of the fingers and thumb
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What does the extensor retinaculum do?
options: Holds the extensor tendons against the back of the wrist
Covers and protects the tendons in the palm
Forms the roof of the carpal tunnel
Spreads the extensor pull over the back of each finger
questions.why: The extensor retinaculum is a band of thickened deep fascia that wraps across the back of the wrist. The extensor tendons pass beneath it on their way to the hand, and it keeps them close to the bones so they do not lift away like a bowstring when the wrist extends. Retinaculum comes from a word meaning a band that holds something back.
notes: Correct. The extensor retinaculum keeps the extensor tendons in place on the back of the wrist.

Covering and protecting the tendons in the palm is the role of the palmar aponeurosis, the triangular sheet of deep fascia continuous with palmaris longus. Choose it if the question asked about the palm.
The roof of the carpal tunnel is the flexor retinaculum, on the front of the wrist. Pick this if the question named the flexor retinaculum.
Spreading the extensor pull over each finger is the job of the extensor expansion, the tendon hood on the back of each finger. Pick it if the question asked where extensor digitorum inserts.
questions.answerText: Holds the extensor tendons against the back of the wrist
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which description fits the palmar aponeurosis?
options: A band across the back of the wrist that holds the extensor tendons in place
A flattened tendon hood over the back of each finger
A fibrous band across the front of the carpal bones that roofs the carpal tunnel
A triangular sheet of deep fascia in the palm, continuous with palmaris longus
questions.why: The palmar aponeurosis is a tough, triangular layer of deep fascia lying just under the skin of the palm. Its narrow end at the wrist is continuous with the tendon of palmaris longus, and it fans out toward the bases of the fingers. It protects the tendons, vessels and nerves beneath it and gives the palm a firm surface for gripping.
notes: A band across the back of the wrist holding the extensor tendons is the extensor retinaculum. Choose it if the question asked about the dorsal wrist.
A tendon hood over the back of each finger is the extensor expansion. Pick it if the question asked where extensor digitorum, the lumbricals and the interossei insert.
A band across the front of the carpal bones that roofs the carpal tunnel is the flexor retinaculum. Pick it if the question asked about the carpal tunnel.
Correct. The palmar aponeurosis is the triangular fascia of the palm, tensed by palmaris longus.
questions.answerText: A triangular sheet of deep fascia in the palm, continuous with palmaris longus
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which tendon forms the medial (ulnar) border of the anatomical snuffbox?
options: Flexor carpi radialis
Extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor pollicis longus
Abductor pollicis longus
questions.why: The anatomical snuffbox is the small hollow on the thumb side of the back of the wrist that appears when you extend the thumb. Its medial (ulnar) border is the tendon of extensor pollicis longus, and its lateral border is formed by the tendons of abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis. The scaphoid lies in its floor and the radial artery crosses it.
notes: Flexor carpi radialis runs on the front of the wrist, where its tendon is the landmark for the radial pulse. It does not border the snuffbox, which is on the back of the wrist.
Extensor pollicis brevis forms part of the lateral border of the snuffbox, together with abductor pollicis longus. Pick it if the question asked about the lateral border.
Correct. Extensor pollicis longus forms the medial border of the snuffbox.
Abductor pollicis longus forms the lateral border of the snuffbox with extensor pollicis brevis. Choose it if the question asked about the lateral border.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: What is the extensor expansion?
options: A tough band over the front of the carpal bones
A band across the back of the wrist that keeps the extensor tendons from lifting away
A triangular sheet of deep fascia across the palm
A flattened tendon hood over the back of each finger
questions.why: Each extensor digitorum tendon flattens out over the back of its finger into a hood called the extensor expansion (also called the dorsal digital expansion). The hood wraps the sides of the proximal phalanx and carries the extensor pull out to the middle and distal phalanges. The lumbricals and interossei also attach to it, which is how these small hand muscles help straighten the finger joints.
notes: A tough band over the front of the carpal bones is the flexor retinaculum, the roof of the carpal tunnel. Pick it if the question asked about the carpal tunnel.
A band across the back of the wrist holding the tendons down is the extensor retinaculum. Pick it if the question asked what keeps the extensor tendons from bowstringing.
A triangular sheet of deep fascia in the palm is the palmar aponeurosis. Choose it if the question asked about the fascia that palmaris longus tenses.
Correct. The extensor expansion is the tendon hood on the back of each finger.
questions.answerText: A flattened tendon hood over the back of each finger
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: When the thumb is extended, which two tendons form the lateral (radial) border of the anatomical snuffbox?
options: Extensor pollicis brevis and extensor pollicis longus
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
Extensor pollicis longus and extensor indicis
questions.why: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis arise next to each other on the posterior radius and run together to the thumb, so their tendons lie side by side and form the lateral border of the snuffbox. Extensor pollicis longus takes a separate path from the ulna and forms the opposite, medial border. The hollow between them deepens when the thumb is extended because all three tendons tighten.
notes: This pair takes one tendon from each border. Extensor pollicis brevis is lateral and extensor pollicis longus is medial, so together they bracket the snuffbox rather than forming one border.
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus are on the front of the wrist. Choose them if the question asked about tendons you can see on the palm side of the wrist.
Correct. Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis form the lateral border.

Extensor pollicis longus forms the medial border alone, and extensor indicis heads to the index finger, not the thumb. Pick extensor pollicis longus by itself if the question asked about the medial border.
questions.answerText: Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which structure crossing the front of the wrist does not pass through the carpal tunnel?
options: Flexor digitorum profundus tendons
Median nerve
Flexor pollicis longus tendon
Ulnar nerve
questions.why: The ulnar nerve crosses the wrist on the little finger side next to the pisiform, passing superficial to the flexor retinaculum rather than under it. That keeps it outside the carpal tunnel. The median nerve and the long flexor tendons of the fingers and thumb all pass beneath the retinaculum, inside the tunnel.
notes: The four flexor digitorum profundus tendons pass through the carpal tunnel beneath the superficialis tendons. Pick them if the question asked which tendons in the tunnel bend the fingertips.

The median nerve runs through the carpal tunnel beneath the flexor retinaculum, which is why it is compressed in carpal tunnel syndrome. Pick it if the question asked which nerve passes through the tunnel.
The flexor pollicis longus tendon is one of the nine tendons in the carpal tunnel, running on its thumb side. Choose it if the question asked which tendon in the tunnel bends the thumb tip.
Correct. The ulnar nerve passes superficial to the flexor retinaculum, outside the tunnel.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which muscles form the medial and lateral borders of the cubital fossa?
options: Biceps brachii medially and triceps brachii laterally
Flexor carpi ulnaris medially and extensor carpi ulnaris laterally
Pronator teres medially and brachioradialis laterally
Brachioradialis medially and pronator teres laterally
questions.why: The cubital fossa is the triangular hollow on the front of the elbow. Its upper border is an imaginary line between the medial and lateral epicondyles, its medial border is pronator teres, and its lateral border is brachioradialis. The two muscles converge below the elbow to form the point of the triangle.
notes: Biceps brachii lies in the anterior arm and its tendon runs through the middle of the fossa, while triceps brachii is on the back of the arm. Neither forms a border.
Flexor carpi ulnaris and extensor carpi ulnaris both run down the ulnar side of the forearm, far from the front of the elbow. They do not outline the cubital fossa.
Correct. Pronator teres forms the medial border and brachioradialis the lateral border.
This swaps the two borders. Pronator teres starts at the medial epicondyle, so it must be the medial border, and brachioradialis runs down the thumb side of the forearm.
questions.answerText: Pronator teres medially and brachioradialis laterally
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: From lateral to medial, what is the order of the main structures inside the cubital fossa?
options: Biceps brachii tendon, brachial artery, median nerve
Biceps brachii tendon, median nerve, brachial artery
Brachial artery, biceps brachii tendon, median nerve
Median nerve, brachial artery, biceps brachii tendon
questions.why: From lateral to medial, the cubital fossa contains the tendon of biceps brachii, then the brachial artery, then the median nerve. The artery lies right beside the biceps tendon, which is why you feel for the brachial pulse just medial to that tendon when taking a blood pressure. The brachial artery divides into the radial and ulnar arteries just below the elbow.
notes: Correct. Tendon, artery, nerve runs from lateral to medial.
This swaps the artery and the nerve. The median nerve is the most medial structure, with the brachial artery between it and the biceps tendon.
This places the artery lateral to the biceps tendon. The tendon is the most lateral of the three, and the artery lies on its medial side.
This is the correct order reversed, running from medial to lateral. Pick it if the question asked for the order starting on the medial side.
questions.answerText: Biceps brachii tendon, brachial artery, median nerve
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the palmar and dorsal interossei?
options: Palmar interossei abduct the fingers away from the middle finger; dorsal interossei adduct them toward it
Palmar interossei adduct the fingers toward the middle finger; dorsal interossei abduct them away from it
Both groups flex the fingertips and differ only in location
Palmar interossei move the thumb; dorsal interossei move the little finger
questions.why: Both sets of interossei lie between the metacarpals, but they pull in opposite directions. The palmar interossei adduct, drawing the fingers together toward the middle finger, and the dorsal interossei abduct, spreading them away from it. The course notes use PAD and DAB to keep them straight: palmar adduct, dorsal abduct.
notes: This reverses the two actions. Remember PAD for palmar adduct and DAB for dorsal abduct.
Correct. Palmar adduct and dorsal abduct (PAD and DAB).
Neither group reaches the distal phalanx, so neither flexes the fingertips. That job belongs to flexor digitorum profundus.
The interossei act on the fingers, measured from the middle finger. The thumb is moved by the thenar muscles and adductor pollicis, and the little finger by the hypothenar muscles.
questions.answerText: Palmar interossei adduct the fingers toward the middle finger; dorsal interossei abduct them away from it
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the thenar and hypothenar groups?
options: Thenar muscles extend the thumb; hypothenar muscles extend the little finger
Thenar muscles arise in the forearm; hypothenar muscles lie entirely within the hand
Thenar muscles form the thumb pad and move the thumb; hypothenar muscles form the little finger pad and move the little finger
Thenar muscles form the bulge on the little finger side; hypothenar muscles form the bulge at the base of the thumb
questions.why: The two groups mirror each other on opposite sides of the palm. The thenar group (abductor pollicis brevis, flexor pollicis brevis, opponens pollicis) forms the pad at the base of the thumb, and the hypothenar group (abductor digiti minimi, flexor digiti minimi brevis, opponens digiti minimi) forms the pad on the little finger side. Each has an abductor, a short flexor and an opponens.
notes: Neither group contains an extensor. Thumb extension comes from extensor pollicis longus and brevis in the posterior forearm, and little finger extension from extensor digitorum and extensor digiti minimi.
Both groups are intrinsic muscles that lie entirely within the hand. The thumb muscles that arise in the forearm, such as abductor pollicis longus, are not part of the thenar group.
Correct. Thenar is the thumb side and hypothenar is the little finger side, with matching sets of muscles.
This swaps the two groups. The thenar eminence is the pad at the base of the thumb, and the hypothenar eminence is the pad on the little finger side of the palm.
questions.answerText: Thenar muscles form the thumb pad and move the thumb; hypothenar muscles form the little finger pad and move the little finger
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which thenar muscle is named for the movement of bringing the thumb pad across the palm to meet the fingertips?
options: Abductor pollicis brevis
Flexor pollicis brevis
Adductor pollicis
Opponens pollicis
questions.why: Bringing the thumb pad across the palm to touch the fingertips is called opposition, and opponens means the one that opposes. Opponens pollicis inserts on metacarpal 1 and rotates it so the pad of the thumb faces the fingers. This movement is what lets you pinch and pick up small objects.
notes: Abductor pollicis brevis moves the thumb away from the palm. Its name describes abduction, so pick it if the question asked which thenar muscle lifts the thumb away from the hand.
Flexor pollicis brevis bends the thumb at its knuckle. Choose it if the question asked which thenar muscle flexes the metacarpophalangeal joint of the thumb.
Adductor pollicis pulls the thumb toward the palm, as in pinching a key against the side of the index finger. Pick it if the question described squeezing the thumb against the hand.
Correct. Opponens pollicis is named for opposition of the thumb.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: The lumbricals flex the knuckles but extend the finger joints. Which attachments explain this?
options: They arise from the metacarpals and insert on the palmar side of the distal phalanges
They arise from the medial epicondyle and insert on the middle phalanges
They arise from flexor digitorum profundus tendons and insert on the extensor expansions
They arise from the extensor digitorum tendons and insert on the flexor retinaculum
questions.why: Each lumbrical starts on a tendon of flexor digitorum profundus in the palm and runs along the thumb side of the knuckle to join the extensor expansion on the back of the finger. Because it passes in front of the knuckle (metacarpophalangeal joint), it flexes that joint, and because it pulls on the extensor expansion beyond the knuckle, it straightens the interphalangeal joints. Origin and insertion together explain the split action.
notes: A muscle inserting on the palmar side of the distal phalanges would bend the fingertips, which is the action of flexor digitorum profundus. The lumbricals straighten the finger joints instead.
The medial epicondyle and middle phalanges are the attachments of flexor digitorum superficialis, a forearm muscle that flexes the finger joints rather than extending them.
Correct. A flexor tendon origin and an extensor expansion insertion give the lumbricals their split action.

The lumbricals arise from flexor tendons, not extensor tendons, and the flexor retinaculum is a band at the wrist that no hand muscle uses as its insertion. This choice reverses their origin and misplaces their insertion.
questions.answerText: They arise from flexor digitorum profundus tendons and insert on the extensor expansions
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: The flexor retinaculum stretches across the front of the wrist between which bony attachments?
options: The styloid processes of the radius and ulna on the back of the wrist
The medial and lateral epicondyles of the humerus
The bases of metacarpals 2 and 5 on the back of the hand
Pisiform and hamate medially, scaphoid and trapezium laterally
questions.why: The flexor retinaculum is a strong fibrous band that bridges the carpal bones on the palmar side. It attaches medially to the pisiform and the hook of the hamate and laterally to the scaphoid and trapezium, turning the curved front of the carpal bones into a closed tunnel. Its arch keeps the long flexor tendons close to the wrist so they do not bowstring when the wrist flexes.
notes: The back of the wrist is where the extensor retinaculum lies, not the flexor retinaculum. Choose a dorsal answer only if the question asked about the band holding the extensor tendons.
The medial and lateral epicondyles are at the elbow, where an imaginary line between them forms the upper border of the cubital fossa. Pick them if the question asked about the cubital fossa.
The bases of the metacarpals are farther out in the hand and on the back they receive the wrist extensors. They are not the anchors of a band that roofs the carpal tunnel.
Correct. The flexor retinaculum spans from the pisiform and hamate to the scaphoid and trapezium.
questions.answerText: Pisiform and hamate medially, scaphoid and trapezium laterally
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Besides extensor digitorum, which intrinsic hand muscles insert into the extensor expansions of the fingers?
options: Lumbricals and interossei
Flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus
Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris
Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis
questions.why: The extensor expansion is the tendon hood on the back of each finger. Besides receiving the extensor digitorum tendon, it receives the small intrinsic muscles of the palm, the lumbricals and the interossei. Pulling on this hood from the side is how these little muscles help straighten the interphalangeal joints even though they lie in the palm.
notes: Correct. The lumbricals and interossei join the extensor expansions.
Flexor digitorum superficialis and profundus insert on the palmar side of the middle and distal phalanges. They bend the fingers and never reach the back of the finger.
Flexor carpi radialis and flexor carpi ulnaris are forearm muscles that insert on metacarpal and carpal bones. They move the wrist, not the fingers.
Abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis insert on the thumb, at metacarpal 1 and the proximal phalanx. Pick them if the question asked about the snuffbox.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: The middle finger has a dorsal interosseous on each side but no palmar interosseous. Why does this arrangement make sense?
options: The middle finger is adducted by the lumbricals instead of the interossei
The middle finger is the reference line, so moving it to either side is abduction
The middle finger is moved sideways only by the extensor digitorum tendon
The middle finger cannot move side to side at all, so it needs no interossei
questions.why: Adduction in the hand means moving a finger toward the line through the middle finger. The middle finger cannot move toward itself, so it never adducts, and any sideways movement in either direction takes it away from its resting line, which counts as abduction. That is why it has two dorsal interossei (abductors) and no palmar interosseous (the adductors).
notes: The lumbricals flex the knuckles and extend the finger joints. They do not move the fingers side to side, and the middle finger has nothing to adduct toward.
Correct. Because it is the reference line, every sideways movement of the middle finger is abduction.
Extensor digitorum straightens the fingers and does not move them sideways. Side-to-side movement of the fingers comes from the interossei.
The middle finger can move side to side, which you can check by wiggling it toward the index and ring fingers. The dorsal interossei on each side produce that movement.
questions.answerText: The middle finger is the reference line, so moving it to either side is abduction
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A worker's flexor tendon sheaths swell inside the carpal tunnel, and she develops tingling in the thumb, index and middle fingers. Why is the median nerve compressed while the ulnar nerve is spared?
options: The median nerve runs on the back of the wrist, under the extensor retinaculum with the tendons
Only the median nerve runs under the flexor retinaculum; the ulnar nerve passes superficial to it
The ulnar nerve runs through the tunnel too but is cushioned by thicker connective tissue
The ulnar nerve ends in the forearm and never reaches the wrist or the hand
questions.why: The carpal tunnel has rigid walls: carpal bones below and the flexor retinaculum above. The median nerve travels through it with nine flexor tendons, so when the tendon sheaths swell, the nerve is squeezed against the retinaculum. The ulnar nerve crosses the wrist superficial to the flexor retinaculum, outside the tunnel, so the swelling does not reach it.
notes: The median nerve crosses the front of the wrist, not the back. The structures under the extensor retinaculum are the extensor tendons.
Correct. Only the median nerve shares the tunnel with the swollen tendons.
The ulnar nerve does not travel in the carpal tunnel at all. This choice comes from assuming every nerve to the hand passes through the tunnel.
The ulnar nerve continues past the wrist into the hand, passing beside the pisiform. It is spared because of its path, not because it stops early.
questions.answerText: Only the median nerve runs under the flexor retinaculum; the ulnar nerve passes superficial to it
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: During a blood draw from the median cubital vein, a needle pushed too deep at the front of the elbow could reach which structures lying just under the bicipital aponeurosis?
options: The cephalic vein and the basilic vein
The radial nerve and the deep brachial artery in the radial groove
The brachial artery and the median nerve
The axillary artery and the axillary nerve
questions.why: The median cubital vein lies superficially across the cubital fossa. Directly beneath it, separated only by the thin bicipital aponeurosis, lie the brachial artery and the median nerve. That is why a blood draw is taken here and why the needle is angled shallowly and carefully.
notes: The cephalic and basilic veins are superficial veins that the median cubital vein connects. They lie at the same shallow level as the vein being drawn from, not deep to the aponeurosis.
The radial nerve and deep brachial artery travel together in the radial groove on the back of the humerus. Choose them if the question asked what is at risk with a mid-shaft humerus fracture.
Correct. The brachial artery and median nerve lie just under the bicipital aponeurosis.
The axillary artery and axillary nerve are in the armpit and around the surgical neck of the humerus, far above the elbow. Pick them if the question asked about the shoulder region.
questions.answerText: The brachial artery and the median nerve
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A student wants to feel the radial artery pulse in the anatomical snuffbox. After extending her thumb, where should she press?
options: Between the flexor carpi ulnaris tendon and the pisiform on the little finger side
Between the flexor carpi radialis tendon and the palmaris longus tendon at the front
In the hollow between extensor pollicis longus and the two lateral thumb tendons
Between the extensor digitorum tendons to the index and middle fingers on the back
questions.why: Extending the thumb tightens the three thumb tendons and opens the snuffbox between them, with extensor pollicis longus on the medial side and abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis on the lateral side. The radial artery crosses the floor of this hollow on its way to the back of the hand, lying over the scaphoid. Pressing gently in the hollow lets you feel its pulse against the bone.
notes: The flexor carpi ulnaris tendon and pisiform are on the little finger side of the front of the wrist, where the ulnar artery runs. Pick this spot if the question asked where to feel the ulnar pulse.
On the front of the wrist the radial pulse is felt lateral to the flexor carpi radialis tendon, not between it and palmaris longus. This spot is also on the palm side, not in the snuffbox.
Correct. The radial artery crosses the snuffbox between these tendons.
The extensor digitorum tendons fan out over the back of the hand toward the fingers, well away from the base of the thumb. No major pulse is taken between them.
questions.answerText: In the hollow between extensor pollicis longus and the two lateral thumb tendons
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: A clinician asks a patient to grip a sheet of paper between two straightened fingers while she tries to pull it away. Which muscles is this testing?
options: Lumbricals
Palmar interossei
Dorsal interossei
Hypothenar muscles
questions.why: Holding paper between two straightened fingers requires squeezing the fingers together, which is adduction toward the middle finger. Adduction of the fingers is the job of the palmar interossei (PAD: palmar adduct). If they are weak, the paper slides out easily.
notes: The lumbricals flex the knuckles and straighten the finger joints, producing the tabletop position. Choose them if the patient were asked to hold that position.
Correct. Squeezing the fingers together tests the palmar interossei.
The dorsal interossei do the opposite movement, spreading the fingers apart. Pick them if the clinician asked the patient to spread the fingers against resistance.
The hypothenar muscles move only the little finger. They do not squeeze two fingers together, so pick them only for a test of little finger movement.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: In an older patient, a band of thickened tissue in the palm slowly pulls the ring and little fingers into a bent position that he cannot straighten. Which structure has thickened and shortened?
options: Extensor retinaculum
Extensor expansion
Palmar aponeurosis
Flexor retinaculum
questions.why: This is Dupuytren contracture, a gradual thickening and shortening of the palmar aponeurosis, the triangular sheet of deep fascia under the skin of the palm. Its bands extend toward the fingers, so as they tighten they draw the fingers, most often the ring and little fingers, into flexion at the knuckles. The muscles and tendons are not the cause; the shortened fascia itself holds the fingers bent.
notes: The extensor retinaculum is on the back of the wrist and holds down the extensor tendons. Pick it if the scenario described tendons bowstringing on the back of the wrist.
The extensor expansion is the tendon hood on the back of each finger. Damage to it would leave a finger unable to straighten actively, but it would not create a thick band in the palm.
Correct. A thickened, shortened palmar aponeurosis pulls the fingers into flexion.
The flexor retinaculum is the band across the front of the wrist that roofs the carpal tunnel. Its problems cause nerve compression in the tunnel, not a band in the palm pulling the fingers down.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: After an injury to the back of the wrist, the extensor tendons lift away from the bones like a bowstring whenever the patient extends the wrist. Which structure was most likely torn?
options: Palmar aponeurosis
Extensor expansion
Flexor retinaculum
Extensor retinaculum
questions.why: The extensor retinaculum is a band across the back of the wrist that holds the extensor tendons close to the bones. When the wrist extends, the tendons pull in a straight line between their origin and insertion, and the retinaculum is what stops them from lifting off the curve of the wrist. If it is torn, the tendons spring up under the skin, a sign called bowstringing.
notes: The palmar aponeurosis is the fascia of the palm on the front of the hand. It does not hold down any tendons on the back of the wrist.
The extensor expansion is the tendon hood over each finger, beyond the wrist. Damage to it would affect straightening of that finger, not the position of the tendons at the wrist.
The flexor retinaculum does the same job on the front of the wrist for the flexor tendons. Pick it if the flexor tendons bowstrung when the wrist flexed.
Correct. A torn extensor retinaculum lets the extensor tendons bowstring.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which list names the four muscles of the quadriceps femoris?
options: Rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, sartorius
Rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius
Biceps femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius
Rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, gracilis, vastus intermedius
questions.why: Quadriceps means four heads. The quadriceps femoris on the front of the thigh is made of the rectus femoris in the middle and three vastus muscles: the vastus lateralis on the outer side, the vastus medialis on the inner side, and the vastus intermedius deep to the rectus femoris. All four join in the quadriceps tendon, which surrounds the patella and continues as the patellar ligament to the tibial tuberosity.
notes: The sartorius is the long strap muscle that crosses the front of the thigh diagonally from the hip to the medial knee. It is in the anterior thigh but is not part of the quadriceps, so it fits a question about the longest muscle in the body.
Correct. These are the four heads of the quadriceps femoris.
The biceps femoris is a hamstring muscle on the back of the thigh. Students pick it because its name ends in femoris, but it would be the answer for the lateral hamstring.
The gracilis is a slender muscle of the medial thigh, in the adductor group. It would fit a question about the medial compartment, not the quadriceps.
questions.answerText: Rectus femoris, vastus lateralis, vastus medialis, vastus intermedius
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which list names the three hamstring muscles?
options: Biceps femoris, semitendinosus, gastrocnemius
Rectus femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus
Biceps femoris, semitendinosus, semimembranosus
Biceps femoris, gracilis, semimembranosus
questions.why: The hamstrings are the three muscles of the posterior thigh. The biceps femoris lies on the lateral side, while the semitendinosus and the semimembranosus lie on the medial side, with the semitendinosus more superficial. Running behind both the hip and the knee, the group extends the thigh at the hip and flexes the knee.
notes: The gastrocnemius is a calf muscle of the posterior leg. It lies just below the hamstrings and also helps flex the knee, but it belongs to the leg and is the answer for a calf question.
The rectus femoris is part of the quadriceps on the front of the thigh, the group that opposes the hamstrings. Pick it for a question about the quadriceps.
Correct. The biceps femoris, semitendinosus and semimembranosus are the hamstrings.
The gracilis is a slender muscle of the medial thigh in the adductor group. It sits near the semitendinosus at the knee, which is why students mix them up, but it is not a hamstring.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which gluteal muscle is the largest, and what is its main action?
options: Gluteus medius; extends the thigh
Gluteus maximus; flexes the thigh
Gluteus medius; abducts the thigh
Gluteus maximus; extends the thigh
questions.why: The gluteus maximus is the largest and most superficial gluteal muscle, forming most of the bulk of the buttock. It runs from the posterior ilium, sacrum, and coccyx to the gluteal tuberosity of the femur and the iliotibial (IT) band, passing behind the hip, so its main action is to extend the thigh at the hip. It is the main extensor for climbing stairs and rising from a chair.
notes: The gluteus medius lies partly under the gluteus maximus and is smaller. Its main action is abduction, so pairing it with extension gets both the muscle and the action wrong.

The gluteus maximus is the right muscle, but it extends the thigh rather than flexing it. Flexing the thigh at the hip is the job of the iliopsoas on the front, which is the answer for a hip flexion question.
The gluteus medius does abduct the thigh, but it is not the largest gluteal muscle. Choose this pairing for a question about which gluteal muscle keeps the pelvis level when you stand on one leg.
Correct. The gluteus maximus is the largest gluteal muscle and extends the thigh.
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: Which statement correctly compares the actions of the quadriceps and the hamstrings at the knee?
options: Quadriceps flex the knee; hamstrings extend the knee
Both groups flex the knee as synergists
Both groups extend the knee as synergists
Quadriceps extend the knee; hamstrings flex the knee
questions.why: The quadriceps lie on the front of the thigh and pull on the tibia through the patellar ligament, straightening (extending) the knee. The hamstrings lie on the back of the thigh and pass behind the knee to attach on the tibia and fibula, so they bend (flex) it. Because they produce opposite actions at the same joint, the two groups are antagonists of each other.
notes: This reverses the two groups. A muscle on the front of the knee pulls the leg straight, so the quadriceps are the extensors, and the hamstrings behind the knee are the flexors.
The hamstrings do flex the knee, but the quadriceps do the opposite. Students pick this when they remember that both groups cross the knee but forget they pull on opposite sides of it.
Synergists are muscles that help each other with the same action, but these two groups work in opposite directions at the knee. Only the quadriceps extend it.
Correct. The quadriceps extend the knee and the hamstrings flex it.
questions.answerText: Quadriceps extend the knee; hamstrings flex the knee
review: territory set from the card's topic

questions.q: As you lower yourself slowly from standing into a chair, your knees bend under your body weight. Which muscle group works to control that bending and keep you from dropping?
options: Adductor group
Gastrocnemius and soleus
Hamstrings
Quadriceps femoris
questions.why: When you sit down slowly, gravity is what bends your knees. To keep from dropping, the knee extensors, the quadriceps, stay active while lengthening, braking the knee flexion that gravity produces. That is why your thighs feel the effort in a slow squat even though your knees are bending.
